**VERSE 10.—You will never sin.** That is, you will attain eternal life, where you will no longer sin. Or, you will avoid grave sins; whoever commits them will not have an inheritance in the kingdom of Christ. With the Lord’s help, the person who has devoted himself to the virtues mentioned above remains free from them. No one, however, can exist without venial sins.

**VERSE 11.—For thus.** (BEDA.) Ezekiel, speaking of a building established on a mountain, etc., up to and including: “and the God of gods will be seen in Zion” (Psalm 83).

**VERSE 12.—I will always remind you of these things.** So that the entrance to the Holy of Holies may be open to you, I will warn you again and again, and I will always be beginning, because there will never be an end to admonition. Therefore, since it is not burdensome for me to repeat these things frequently, let it not be burdensome for you to hear them frequently.

And indeed, knowing these things. (BEDE.) Why does he wish to admonish those who know and have been confirmed? Clearly, so that they may exercise in works the knowledge they possess and keep firmly in mind the truth by whose presence they have been confirmed, lest at some point they fall away from the simplicity and chastity of the faith through teachers of error.

**VERSE 13.—But I consider it right, etc.** I admonish you because I consider it right to do so, since the Lord kindly called [Col. 0690C] me, confirmed me, and commanded me to confirm others, saying, “Strengthen your brothers.” I therefore arouse you, as though you were sleeping, to the matters mentioned above, always remaining diligently attentive to admonishing you.

**VERSE 14.—The putting off of my tabernacle.** (BEDE.) He aptly calls it not death but a putting off, because for God’s servants to cast off the restraints of the flesh is like travelers, once their journey is completed, entering their own home instead of a tent for habitation; or like soldiers in the field returning to their homeland after the enemy has been overthrown.

**VERSE 15.—But I will take care.** Because I am soon to depart, therefore, while I live, I will take care that you frequently—namely, whenever the false teachers press upon you and wish to draw you away—keep these things in memory [Col. 0690D] after my death, when you will no longer have me present as your teacher. I do not mean that you should possess them in some casual manner, but that you should make their memory effective by fulfilling them in practice and teaching them to others.

**After my death, etc.** The departure of the saints is so called when they go out to meet the bridegroom.

**VERSE 16.—For we did not follow cleverly devised tales, etc.** (BEDE.) Here he also touches upon pagans and heretics. Pagans did not hesitate to call gods whatever pleased them. Heretics, after receiving the mysteries of the true God, no longer attended to the divine [Col. 0691A] Scriptures, but instead strove to twist them into an erroneous meaning by interpreting them badly.

**But having become eyewitnesses, etc.** The Lord’s Transfiguration and his glory were signs of his resurrection and ours. Through Elijah, who appeared with him, is understood the resurrection of those who lived before the Law; through Moses, that of those who lived under the Law; and through Peter, James, and John, that of those who live under grace. Or, through Moses, who was dead, the resurrection of the dead; through the living men, that of the living.

**VERSE 19.—And we have something more reliable.** What I told you is not a fable but certain; and it was declared not only by these signs, but also, for the confirmation of our preaching, we have the prophetic word of David: “The Lord said to me, ‘You are my Son’” (Psalm 2), and so forth. It is more reliable than the words of the other prophets [Col. 0691B] because he prophesied more clearly than the others concerning Christ.

**To which you do well to attend.** (BEDE.) So that you may have the light of knowledge, etc., until the point that, in comparison with the life to come, we need a lamp.

**VERSE 20.—Understanding this first.** Attend to the prophetic word, for it comes from God. This can be demonstrated by the fact that prophecy is not written in such words or in such a manner of speech as people use in ordinary conversation, nor in the manner in which secular writings are composed and interpreted. Indeed, the speech of the prophets does not proceed from their own will or that of their hearers, but from the will of the Holy Spirit who spoke through them.

**VERSE 21.—For prophecy never came by human will.** (BEDE.) Just as it was not always in the prophets’ power to possess the Spirit [Col. 0691C] or to proclaim future events, so it was not in their power to teach whatever they wished; they spoke only what they had learned from the Spirit. These things are said so that no one may interpret the Scriptures according to his own pleasure.

## CHAPTER II

**VERSE 1.—Destruction.** They rightly bring destruction upon themselves who deny their Redeemer, or who preach him not as the truth reveals him but as they themselves invent him. Being therefore estranged from the Redeemer, they can expect nothing more certain than the pit.

**VERSE 2.—The way of truth will be blasphemed.** (BEDE.) Through heretics, the way of truth is accustomed to be blasphemed not only among those whom they associate with themselves after seducing them into their heresy, but also among those whom they provoke to hatred of the Christian name by their most impure [Col. 0691D] deeds and by the detestable sacrifices or mysteries they perform. The uninstructed come to suppose that all Christians are devoted to such crimes.

**VERSE 4.—For if God did not spare the angels.** (BEDE.) If God handed over the apostate angels to the punishments of hell, etc., until they were carried away into the depths of the abyss.

**VERSE 5.—The original world.** (BEDE.) The world after the flood is the same world as before it, etc., until the righteous receive the glory of life.

**VERSE 6.—And the cities.** These cities were reduced to fire in two ways: first, he reduced them to ashes by burning them together with the neighboring lands; and later, when he covered the places of the conflagration with the waters of the Dead Sea, he still wished the surrounding region to preserve the appearance of its ancient punishment. For exceedingly beautiful fruits grow there, and they arouse in those who see them a desire to eat them. If you pluck one, it breaks apart and dissolves into ash, producing smoke as though it were still burning. **Into ash.** The fire that once punished the Sodomites signifies what the wicked will suffer without end. The smoking earth and the beautiful fruits that contain ash and stench within indicate that carnal desire, although it delights fools, stores up for itself nothing but burning in invisible things, or that the smoke of their torments may rise for ages of ages.

**VERSE 7.—Lot, who was oppressed.** (BEDE.) The unjust deeds and words of his neighbors tormented the righteous man. He saw them [Col. 0692B] but could not correct them, while he preserved himself in good works. He did not stain himself by the crimes he saw or heard. He is likewise called righteous in sight and hearing because they saw nothing in him and heard nothing about him except what belonged to righteousness.

**VERSE 9.—The unrighteous.** The false teachers and their followers; therefore, do not follow them.

**For the day of judgment.** (BEDE.) Even before the day of judgment, when released from the body they suffer punishments, and at the judgment they await more severe ones, when they will be tormented in body and soul.

**VERSE 11.—Where angels are.** The unrighteous will be tormented there where the evil angels are—those who had first acted proudly against God and were therefore punished. They no longer bear, but rather cast away, the judgment of taking pride against God. This is detestable against themselves, because they are severely [Col. 0692C] punished for it; and, terrified by the magnitude of their punishments, they now desist from that presumptuous judgment. But these unrighteous people have not yet desisted. Or they will be tormented there, that is, with God, where the non-good angels do not tolerate but avenge anything detestable that is said against them.

**VERSE 13.—The reward of unrighteousness.** (BEDE.) That is, punishment for evil works—especially for those who, while serving the corruption of the flesh and being held by deranged errors, blaspheme the conduct of the righteous and do not cease to slander those who think soundly.

**VERSE 17.—These are.** The false apostles are not to be imitated, because although they may appear useful, there is nothing in them but vanity and uncleanness.

**VERSE 18.—Proud.** Proudly claiming to be righteous, although this is vain; carnally desiring and luxuriously living, they entice those who have withdrawn a little from sins. Although such people resemble them, they nevertheless in some measure avoid their company and refrain to some extent from sins. **In the desires of the flesh, etc.** Everyone is unclean who exalts his heart, so that those who have withdrawn somewhat from sins may return to their error and devote themselves to luxury.

**VERSE 20.—For if, etc., through the knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, etc.** If, after fleeing the defilement of soul and body that the world brings, they are again entangled in those defilements and overcome by them—as they were before baptism—it is evident that their later condition has become worse than the earlier. For they offend God more grievously than before baptism and will suffer greater punishments, because the promises made in baptism have proved false in them.

**VERSE 22.—For what happened to them.** (BEDE.) In Proverbs this is set down with an interpretation, etc., until it makes even tears themselves filthy in the sight of God.

## CHAPTER III

**VERSE 1.—This second letter, behold, I am writing to you.** It is as though he said: “I have already written another letter to repel the false teachers; and, to show you my great concern for you, behold, I am writing this second letter also for the same reason.”

**VERSE 2.—That you may remember.** That is, through those letters you may remember the words that I myself, while present, formerly spoke to you. I mean words received [Col. 0693B] from the holy prophets, which are confirmed by the authority of the holy prophets; and may remember the commandments of the holy apostles, so that you do not abandon the commandments the holy apostles gave you in favor of the preaching of those false teachers—commandments that are also those of the Lord and Savior, since the Lord himself, who came to save us, established these commandments and ordered us to keep them.

**VERSE 5.—It escapes their notice.** (BEDE.) Therefore they say that everything continues in the same way, etc., until the day of judgment and the destruction of ungodly people.

**VERSE 8.—But do not overlook this one thing.** Having established that there truly will be a judgment, he shows how effective it will be. If the false teachers say to you, “You may do whatever you wish, because so much time remains until the day of judgment that, because of the length of time, the judge will not be able to know many things,” do not believe them. Whatever can happen in a thousand years, he sees just as clearly as what happens in one day. If they say, “By repenting for a thousand years you will not obtain forgiveness of your sins,” do not believe them, because one day of true repentance is as powerful for salvation as a thousand years, as in the case of the thief.

**As a thousand years.** (BEDE.) In the knowledge of divine power, etc., until the point that we need a lamp in comparison with the life to come. Hence it is rightly added [Col. 0694A]:

**VERSE 9.—The Lord is not slow.** Since he sees everything, you can believe that the Lord is not slow to fulfill his promises, because the time has not yet come when what must be fulfilled will be fulfilled. He delays for this reason: so that he may first complete the full number of the elect whom he foresaw. Hence in the Apocalypse: “And it was said to them that they should rest a little longer, until their fellow servants should be completed” (Revelation 6).

**VERSE 10.—The heavens with a great sound.** The heavens—that is, the saints—will be purified by fire if anything in them requires purification.

**The elements.** (BEDE.) The four elements, by which the world consists, etc., until through a temporal punishment they will be changed into something better.

**VERSE 13.—But new heavens.** (BEDE.) He does not say “other” heavens, but that the old and ancient ones will be changed for the better, etc., until we also have this in the prophets: “The light of the lamp shall no longer shine there” (Isaiah 65).

**VERSE 14.—Strive to be found spotless and blameless.** These are the vigils of which it is said: “Blessed are those servants whom the Lord, when he comes, will find watching.” The one who watches is he who keeps himself free from stains; who, insofar as it depends on him, maintains peace with all people; who subjects every enticement of the flesh to the governance of the spirit, enjoying within himself the most blessed peace.

**VERSE 15.—Our brother.** (BEDE.) He says that Paul wrote to them, in which he shows, etc., until through these things they may stir themselves to progress.

**VERSE 16.—Difficult.** In Paul’s letters, which are corrupted by heretics, etc., until some, loosening the reins of luxury [Col. 0694C], and many other things, etc.

**They distort.** (BEDE.) There is no book of the Old or New Testament in which heretics have not perverted something, whether by removing, adding, or changing it. The one remedy for the unlearned is to offer the words of teachers an ear with humble steadfastness. Since heretics do not possess this steadfastness, they are swept from the Church by the wind of pride like light straw, to their own destruction.

[Col. 0693]

# THE FIRST LETTER OF BLESSED JOHN. (G)*

## ARGUMENT

[Col. 0693D]

He explains the meaning of the Word and that God himself is love. He argues at such length that those who whisper against their brothers can neither know God nor become godly, as to prove them murderers, since hatred is the occasion of killing.

## CHAPTER I

**VERSE 1.—That which was from the beginning.** In the nature, or true being, of the Godhead, that which we heard through the Law and the prophets; that which we saw, namely, the one who came visibly as a human being; that which we contemplated, recognizing divinity in the human being; and that which our hands touched—concerning the Word of life. We did not agree with him casually, merely because he was seen in the flesh, but, after careful handling, we bore witness from the Scriptures [Col. 0694D] concerning that very Word. What someone has seen he can announce to others, but what he has fully contemplated he can never explain in words.

**VERSE 2.—We have seen and are witnesses.** We saw him, and by announcing him to unbelievers we became martyrs. **We announce to you.** In this way we heard through them, though we did not see; nevertheless we are no less blessed than they, because it is written: “Blessed are those who have not seen and have believed” (Luke 24).

**VERSE 5.—And this is the announcement.** Why did the Word become flesh? What new thing did he bring to the world? Why did he come to suffer? It was not without purpose. See what he wished to teach: God is light. By this statement he displays the excellence of divine purity, which we are commanded to imitate. Here the Manichaeans are refuted, for they say that God’s nature was conquered and corrupted in battle by the prince [Col. 0695A] of darkness. **We announce, etc.** We have drawn near: light has shone upon us. We were darkness; now, through the light, we are light, and we illuminate others when we announce that sins are forgiven and darkness expelled.

**VERSE 6.—If we say.** Until now he has praised the letter; here he shows how love is to be possessed. **And walk in darkness, etc.** Those who persist in sins and obscure others are not counted among his members. Hence: “What fellowship has Christ with Belial? What partnership has light with darkness?” (2 Corinthians 6).

**VERSE 7.—But if we walk in the light.** We are clean if we walk in the light, but we must not suppose that, as long as we live, we can be completely cleansed from sins. **As he himself, etc.** God is said to be in the light [Col. 0695B] because no higher goodness exists in which he might progress; a human being walks in the light because through works of virtue he progresses toward better things.

**VERSE 8.—If we say, etc.** Those who boast of their merits and say that they are clean also do not possess love. **We have.** He does not say “we had,” lest it appear to refer only to past sins.

**VERSE 9.—May he forgive us our sins.** He calls the sins within us that are more serious “sins,” while he calls the lesser ones “iniquity.”

**VERSE 10.—A liar.** God alone is truthful from himself; a human being is truthful from God and a liar from himself. It is impossible for any saint not at some time to fall into minor sins. Yet they do not cease to be righteous, because with God’s prompt help they rise again.

## CHAPTER II

[Col. 0695C]

**VERSE 1.—My little children, I am writing these things, etc.** Do not adopt a false security because you hear that you are cleansed by God; instead, maintain a beneficial fear. **If anyone sins.** If, because of human frailty, you cannot avoid every vice, take care at least to avoid the greater and more obvious ones, so that temptation may seize you only in a human way. If anyone should fall even after my warning, let him not despair. **An advocate.** He is an advocate only for those who call upon him. Let your sins displease you; cry out, and he himself hears and delivers. **Righteous.** A righteous advocate does not undertake unjust cases; nevertheless, he will defend us as righteous in the judgment if we now accuse ourselves as unrighteous.

[Col. 0695D]

**VERSE 3.—And by this we know.** “To know” or “to recognize” is not always said with reference to knowledge, but also with reference to experience and union with another. We know God when we are united to him. Whoever knows in this way keeps his commandments. **If we keep his commandments.** We must take account of our frailty; we must seek an advocate in our sins. In order to obtain this, let us labor to keep the commandments, through which one comes to knowledge of him.

**VERSE 4.—Whoever says that he knows him, etc.** It is not a great thing merely to know the one God, since the demons also believe and tremble.

**VERSE 7.—Not a new commandment.** The same love is an old commandment because it was commended from the beginning. [Col. 0696A] It is likewise a new commandment because, after darkness has been cast out, it instills a desire for new light.

**VERSE 8.—Which is true.** According to what he promised: that through keeping God’s commandments one comes to knowledge and love of him. **And in him.** It was fulfilled in Christ because he obeyed the Father even unto death, and for that reason he was glorified. **And in you.** Some of you already glory with God through this, and it is truly new because the darkness has already passed away. Darkness belongs to the old person, while light belongs to the new person.

**VERSE 9.—Whoever says, etc.** He specifies what commandment he is referring to, namely love, and how love itself is to be practiced: love of God and of one’s neighbor.

**VERSES 10–11.—Whoever loves his brother is in the light** of knowledge and action; but whoever hates is in the darkness of ignorance. Through that ignorance he walks from vice to vice and does not know—that is, does not foresee—where he is going or to what punishment he is destined. Or, he does not know where he is going because he is ignorant of the path by which he might turn to what is better. This is not because the path is not open, but because darkness has blinded his eyes. Having withdrawn from Christ’s light, he is so obstructed by sins and carnal pleasure that, even when he sees what is good, he does not carry it out.

**VERSE 12.—I am writing to you, etc.** He places first the reason that could draw them away from love of the world: those baptized in the name of Christ and invoking Christ’s name have their sins forgiven. Therefore they must cling more closely to Christ than to the world. **Little children.** Fathers, adolescents, [Col. 0696C] young men. They are called children because their sins are forgiven; fathers because they have known what is ancient; young men because they are strong and have conquered.

**VERSE 13.—Adolescents.** The period of adolescence is slippery because of the incentives of the flesh, but because of the strength of age it is suited to combat. These men overcame the temptations of pleasure through love of God’s word and despised persecutions.

**VERSE 14.—And you have conquered.** At that time young men were drawn by custom to the brothel, but these resisted manfully and conquered.

**VERSE 15.—Do not love the world.** Use the world for necessity, but do not love it for excess. **And do not make provision for the flesh in its desires.** **Do not love the world.** One heart cannot contain two opposing loves. Rooted in love, build nothing upon this root except what accords with love, because you cannot serve two masters. Just as love of God is the source of all virtues, so love of the world is the source of all vices.

**VERSE 16.—Everything that is in the world.** (BEDE.) That is: all lovers of the world possess nothing except these three things, through which, etc., until he did not wish to be exalted above the kingdoms of the world.

**VERSE 17.—But whoever does the will, etc.** Love can also be maintained in this way: if you have not been cast down from the faith and from the other things belonging to God by any impulse of the heretics. And, so that you may hold fast to it, let what you heard from the beginning remain in you.

[Col. 0697A]

**VERSE 18.—Little children, it is the last hour.** Therefore you must persevere, because there are many Antichrists who wish to lead you astray. **As you heard that the Antichrist is coming.** With as great a force and terror as you heard that the Antichrist would come, so violently these people also come. We are in the eleventh hour: the Savior has come in the flesh, and the plague of the Antichrist will follow. He attacks the proclamations of salvation and uproots the vineyard that Christ cultivates. Many members of this most wicked head have already been sent ahead, and you must beware of them, because the end of the world is already near. Or “the last hour” means one resembling the last hour: this persecution resembles the persecution that is to come. **Now there are many Antichrists.** All heretics are Antichrists; so are all who destroy by their [Col. 0697B] deeds the faith they confess in words; all who oppose Christ and, by opposing him, bear witness to his coming head, because the mystery of iniquity is already at work in them.

**VERSE 19.—They went out from us, etc.** Although there are many Antichrists, do not be frightened if they return to Judaism or paganism. Do not therefore think that the Church suffers any loss because of this, since, although they went out from us, they were not truly of us. They could not have gone out unless they had been opposed to Christ. Whoever is not opposed to Christ remains in Christ’s body. They are false within the Church as diseased humors are in the body: when they are expelled, the body is relieved; so, when the wicked leave, the Church is relieved. **But so that they might be revealed.** Many who are not of us receive with us Christ’s sacraments, but [Col. 0697C] temptation proves that they are not of us. When temptation comes upon them, they fly out as though driven by the wind, because they were not grain. All will fly out when the Lord’s threshing floor begins to be winnowed on the day of judgment. Therefore, by God’s permission, some leave the Church before the final separation, showing that they were not part of Christ’s body. In this way it becomes clear that not all who receive Christ’s sacraments with us within the Church are of us, and therefore their separation should not burden you.

**VERSE 20.—But you have an anointing.** While speaking about the heretics, he suddenly turns to his own and says that they have an anointing from the Holy One, thereby showing by contrast that heretics and all Antichrists are deprived of the gift of spiritual grace and do not belong [Col. 0697D] to him who is called Holy by the prophets. **You know all things.** You know the truth of faith and life, taught by the anointing of the Spirit, and you do not need to be taught except to persevere in what you have begun.

**VERSE 21.—And because every lie.** (BEDE.) He had said that every lie is not from the truth, etc., until the point concerning all who disdain obeying Christ’s commandments.

**VERSE 22.—This is the Antichrist, etc.** We have been warned how to recognize the Antichrist: namely, whoever denies Christ, etc. **Whoever denies the Father.** It is useless for someone to confess God as Father while denying the Son who proceeds from God.

**VERSE 24.—What you heard, etc.** If someone says, “Behold, the Christ is here,” or “There,” do not believe him; instead, hold fast to what you heard from the apostles. **And you will abide in the Son and in the Father.** You will be members of the Father and the Son in such a way that you do not fall away from the memory and protection of the Father and the Son. You ought to desire this, so that you may be in the Father and the Son, because from this you will obtain your reward.

**VERSE 25.—This is the promise.** May remembrance of the promised reward make you steadfast in your work.

**VERSE 27.—But as for his anointing.** That is, the Holy Spirit, whose sacrament is represented in visible anointing. Or the anointing is understood as love, which is poured into our hearts through the Holy Spirit who has been given to us; it inflames the heart it fills so that it may keep God’s commandments.

**VERSE 28.—And now, little children, abide.** He inculcates this through frequent repetition so that he may impress it more firmly upon their minds. **Abide in him.** If you possess anything good, attribute it all to him and not to yourselves; attribute what is evil to yourselves and to the devil.

**VERSE 29.—Everyone, etc.** (BEDE.) Perfect righteousness is scarcely found even among angels, etc., until the time when there will no longer be struggle with the flesh but triumph over the enemy.

**From him.** If we have been born from the righteous one, we ought to follow the righteousness of the righteous Father.

## CHAPTER III

**VERSE 1.—See, etc.** Consider carefully with what great and what kind of gifts God has shown his paternal love toward us. He granted that in this world we should be called sons of God in name and in reality, and that in the future we should be sons by possessing an inherited blessedness. **He granted.** God granted love for this purpose: that we might know and be able to love him, not as servants love a master, but as sons love a father. Hence it is said: “But to all who received him, he gave power to become children of God” (John 1).

**VERSE 2.—We are children of God.** It is as though he said: “To be and to be called children of God—what dignity is this?” He answers: “Beloved, we are now children of God.” Through the miracles we perform and the purity of our lives, it is now evident that we are children of God; but whatever exists in the present is little in comparison with the future. **We shall be like him.** When we enjoy the contemplation of the immutable and eternal Godhead, we too shall be immortal and eternal in him—not indeed the same as he is, but like him, because we are creatures made in his likeness. **Because we shall see him.** Insofar as the Word became flesh, the wicked saw him and will see him at the judgment; but only the righteous will see the Word as he was in the beginning with the Father. “The wicked shall be taken away, lest he see the glory of God.”

**VERSE 3.—He sanctifies himself.** (BEDE.) He does not remove free will when he says, etc., until they say to God: “You are my helper; do not forsake me” (Psalm 26).

**VERSE 4.—And sin, etc.** (BEDE.) What the Latins call *legem* (“law”), the Greeks, etc., until those who corrupt the innocence of the natural law are guilty of transgression.

**VERSE 5.—And you know.** So that we—who cannot be free from sins and iniquities [Col. 0699A]—may not despair of salvation, he adds that through Christ we are released from sins. Therefore we have not only been made children of God through grace and hope that we shall be like him, but we are also freed from iniquity, because he appeared for the purpose of taking away sins. No one may excuse himself from this iniquity.

**VERSE 6.—Whoever sins has not seen him.** And whoever remains in him does not sin. Let no one deceive you by saying either that righteousness comes from a human being or that someone can remain in God while committing sin, because all righteousness is from God and all sin is from the devil.

**VERSE 7.—Whoever does righteousness.** That is, whoever possesses the practice and intention of righteousness is indeed righteous, but not from himself. Rather, just as the other is righteous, so this person proceeds from the same root [Col. 0699B]. Righteousness is primary in the one and secondary in the other; natural in the one and received through adoption in the other. The very fact that someone is righteous means that he is righteous from him.

**VERSE 8.—He is from the devil.** (BEDE.) Not by deriving the origin of the flesh from him, as Mani wished, etc., until Christ was born as a human being to dissolve human sins and restore human beings to life.

**VERSE 9.—He does not commit sin.** He is not speaking of every sin. For if we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves; rather, he is speaking of violating love, which one who has within himself the seed of God—that is, the word of God by which he was reborn—cannot commit. **Because his seed is in him.** The true Son of the Father cannot abandon the law. The Father’s law is: “Love one another.”

[Col. 0699C]

**VERSE 12.—Because his works were evil.** Where there is envy, there is no brotherly love. He does not call Cain’s works evil except for envy and hatred of his brother; nor does he call Abel’s works righteous except for love. By this human beings are distinguished. Let no one attend to words, but to deeds. If the heart does not act kindly toward its brothers, it shows what it contains. Cain rightly offered a creature to the Creator, but he did not divide rightly when he thought that the gifts he offered while hating his brother would be pleasing. Abel offered with love, and his offering was pleasing.

**VERSE 14.—We know, etc.** Let no one falsely exalt himself because of his virtues; let no one fear the poverty of his own strength beyond measure. Whoever loves his brother gives clear evidence that he belongs to the lot of the righteous. **Remains in death.** The life of the flesh is the soul; the life of the soul is God. The death of the body is the loss of the spirit [Col. 0699D]; the death of the soul is the loss of God. Whoever therefore loses God through hatred of his brother loses life.

**VERSE 15.—Whoever hates his brother.** Whoever pursues his brother out of hatred provokes him to anger and discord, and thus, insofar as it depends on him, kills him in his soul. If someone were to disregard hatred of his brother, would he not disregard murder in his heart? He does not move his hands to kill, yet he is already held to be a murderer: the other lives, while this one is judged his killer. **He does not have eternal life.** He will be condemned forever with Cain, who is held guilty of this kind of murder because he is divided from his brothers.

**VERSE 16.—By this we know, etc.** After presenting many arguments for the possession of love, he finally sets forth the perfection of love [Col. 0700A] under the example of the Lord’s passion. Peter is urged to possess this love when, in response to the Lord’s question, he professed that he loved him. He was told: “When you grow old, you will stretch out your hands, and another will gird you and lead you where you do not wish to go” (John 21). By these words he was taught to lay down his life for the sheep. “Greater love has no one than this: that someone lay down his life for his friends” (ibid. 15).

**VERSE 17.—Whoever possesses, etc.** If, either because the opportunity does not arise or because of human weakness, it does not happen that we lay down our lives, we ought at least to lay down our possessions for our brothers; this is nourishment for love. Whoever has learned to give away his property will at some time be able to lay down his own life.

**VERSE 18.—Little children, let us not love, etc.** Love is [Col. 0700B] not perfect in the one who does not lay down his life for his brothers, or who at least does not give money. Therefore, if you wish to possess perfect love, little children of the same Father, let us not love in word or tongue. **In word:** pure speech without action is understood. **In tongue:** a multitude of speech is understood, as when some wish to commend their affection through frequently repeated words. **But in deed.** Even if we are mistaken in love through human weakness, we are not mistaken in our reward, because God is greater than our heart and knows with what zeal everything is done. **And in truth.** That is, if we provide benefits with a simple intention—not for boasting or for some temporal advantage, but solely with regard for God.

**VERSE 19.—By this we know, etc.** By loving the truth, we know that we are from the truth [Col. 0700C]—that is, we know that we possess this true love from God, who is truth. Through this love we know that we are in his sight, that is, that we merit his regard; and by this same love we encourage our hearts to devise better works. **And in his sight, etc.** That is, we persuade our hearts to have thoughts worthy of divine sight. For all who intend to do something turn their hearts toward meditating on that very act. But one who thinks evil would conceal it from God if he could; one who thinks good readily persuades his heart to desire that it be revealed to God’s sight. This is a sign of great perfection, when someone rejoices that his action or thought is seen by God.

**VERSE 20.—Because if our heart condemns us.** It is a great thing that through love we have thoughts so clean that we wish to show them to God. Even if our conscience accused us inwardly and we wished to hide from God because we did our good deeds with an evil intention, we could not conceal them from God, because he is greater than our heart and knows everything. Love is therefore effective: it commends us to the one from whom we cannot hide.

**VERSE 22.—And whatever we ask.** This is a great and desirable promise for the faithful. But if anyone is so perverse that he does not delight in heavenly promises, let him at least fear what wisdom thunders with the opposite warning: “Whoever turns his ear away so as not to hear the law—his prayer will be detestable” (Proverbs 28).

[Col. 0701A]

**VERSE 23.—And this is the commandment.** He gives the commandment in the singular and then adds two components, because these cannot be separated.

## CHAPTER IV

**VERSE 1.—Because many.** Many heretics and many schismatics confess that Jesus came in the flesh, but deny it by their deeds because they do not possess love. The Word became flesh through love; whoever does not possess love denies that he came in the flesh, and by this he is shown not to have the Spirit from God. The Spirit of God says that Jesus came in the flesh not through the sound of the tongue, but by loving and doing. Jesus came to gather; the heretic scatters. This person does not have the Spirit of God.

**VERSE 3.—Every spirit, etc.** Many heretics who wished to divide [Col. 0701B] the unity of the Church through perverse doctrine erased this verse from the letter so that they might not be convicted by it of their error. **Dissolves.** Whoever distinguishes God from the human being, divides the members from God, interprets God’s words badly, or withdraws from God by living badly—this person dissolves Jesus.

**VERSE 5.—They are from the world.** These spirits, which are from the world, are not to be loved or listened to. For although they invoke Christ’s name and mark themselves with Christ’s sign, they nevertheless belong to the number of those who desire worldly things and are ignorant of heavenly ones. Therefore they speak from the world, proving by worldly wisdom that God cannot raise a dead person, that a mortal human being cannot have a dwelling in heaven, and other things of this kind.

[Col. 0701C]

**VERSE 7.—Beloved, let us love one another.** He has commended love in many ways; now he approaches its singular praise, in which above all we ought to hear him: “Whoever loves is born from God and knows God, because God is love.” He had said, “Love is from God”; here he adds, “God is love.”

**VERSE 8.—Because God is love.** Love does not differ in God when he is called just and justice, or loving and love. He is not called just from justice, or loving from love, as though he possessed justice or love distinct from himself, but because he is his own justice and his own love.

**VERSE 9.—In this was revealed.** By proving that God is love and that he loves us, he wished to lead us by his example so that we might love one another and come to knowledge [Col. 0701D] of him. Just as God did not wait for us to love him, so we should not wait for others to love us; rather, we should love first. The Father’s love was proved by the fact that he sent the Son; the Son’s love appeared in the fact that he died for us, whom he loved beforehand.

**VERSE 10.—Not as though we.** We did not love first, so that he might love us as though he loved us because our love deserved it. Rather, he loved us first, so that, with his grace going before us, we might love him.

**VERSE 11.—And we ought to love one another.** Love, and do what you wish. Whether you are silent, be silent with love; whether you cry out, cry out with love. Nothing but good can come from this root.

[Col. 0702A]

**VERSE 12.—No one has ever seen God.** (BEDE.) Just as visible things are perceived through the bodily senses, so God is not seen, etc., until the point that, while we are still pilgrims in the body, we should love one another, etc.

**VERSE 13.**—“By this we know.” How shall we know whether we have the Spirit of God? Examine your inmost being: if it is full of charity, you have the Spirit of God. “Because we remain in him.” God remains in us, and we in him; therefore no one should despair of salvation. Even if the illnesses of our sins weigh us down, the almighty physician is able to save. Let us rejoice in hope until we come to the reality.

**VERSE 16.**—“And we have known.” We have seen and testify that God sent his Son, and we have understood why he did this: not because he needed anything, nor because he owed anything, but solely out of charity. Although he had a unique Son, he did not wish him to remain alone; rather, he wished him to have brothers, and he adopted for him those who would possess eternal life with him. [Col. 0702B]

**VERSE 18.**—“There is no fear in charity.” In that charity, namely, which, in imitation of divine goodness, does good even to enemies, there is no fear.

## CHAPTER V

**VERSE 1.**—“Everyone who believes.” He believes who lives in the manner Christ commanded; otherwise even the demons believe. Works apart from faith are either nonexistent or, even if they appear good, empty, because they are outside the way, which is Christ. Truly, whoever loves God loves his brother. For whoever loves God the Father loves God the Son, begotten by the Father; and whoever loves God the Son also loves the sons of God, members of that head. [Col. 0702C]

**VERSE 3.**—“They are not burdensome.” (Bede.) They do not drag one downward like a talent of lead, etc., up to the point where he says that no one should trust in his own strength as though he could conquer the world; then he adds concerning faith:

**VERSE 4.**—“And this is the victory,” etc. It is that faith, namely, which works through love and calls upon God’s help.

**VERSE 5.**—“But who is it?” etc. He determines which faith conquers, namely, the faith of Christ. As though he said: Truly, by faith he conquers the world, because it is not conquered by anything else. “Our faith.” Behold which faith conquers: that which believes him to be true man and true God.

**VERSE 6.**—“This is he,” etc. Because faith and confession of divinity alone are not sufficient for salvation and for conquering the world, he adds what concerns his humanity; for this reason he expressly mentioned blood. [Col. 0702D]

“Spirit”—that is, the human soul which he gave up in his Passion; “water and blood,” which flowed from his side. This could not have happened if he had not possessed the true nature of flesh. Even before the Passion, however, the sweat that became like drops of blood displayed the reality of his flesh. The fact that water and blood flowed vigorously from his already dead side, contrary to nature, testified that the Lord’s body after death would live more perfectly, and that his death would give us life. But the fact that sweat flowed upon the ground like blood signified that by his blood he would wash the Church throughout the whole world.

**VERSE 7.**—“Because there are three.” Through this it is shown that Jesus is truth, true God, and true man. We have certain testimony concerning both: concerning his divinity, through the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit; concerning his humanity, through the soul, the water, and the blood. The Father gave testimony to his divinity when he said, “This is my beloved Son.” The Son himself gave it when he was transfigured on the mountain and displayed both the power of his divinity and the hope of eternal blessedness. The Holy Spirit gave it when he rested upon the baptized Christ in the form of a dove, or when, at the invocation of the name of Christ, he filled the hearts of believers. [Col. 0703A]

**VERSE 10.**—“Whoever believes in the Son of God.” Such a person understands the Father to be truthful in his testimony concerning the Son. Whoever does not believe says that the Father has lied. Therefore the Jews say in vain that they believe in the Father so long as they despise Christ. [Col. 0703B]

“In the Son.” Because the Father testifies concerning the Son, let us believe in the Son. Whoever believes in the Son in such a way that, by desiring what is good, he directs himself toward him has God’s testimony within himself—as though he were saying: God also testifies concerning him that the one who believes in this way will be numbered among the sons of God, since the Son himself promises this in these words: “If anyone ministers to me, my Father will honor him” (John 12). If, then, you have God as witness to your faith, what harm can human disgrace or persecution do you? “If God is for us, who can be against us?” (Romans 8).

**VERSE 11.**—“And this is the testimony.” He testified concerning the Son, and also concerning us, his adopted sons: through his only Son he would grant even to us, already in hope and one day in reality, eternal life. [Col. 0703C]

“And this is life.” (Bede.) In faith and confession of the name, in reception of the sacraments, etc., up to the point where he says that he gives eternal life to his own.

**VERSE 14.**—“And this is the confidence.” He repeats in various ways the same things he had promised above, so as to stir us more vigorously to prayer. “According to his will.” He wishes us to ask for what he wills, or he wishes us to come to prayer as the sort of people he desires us to be. If we desire our own salvation and that of our neighbors, we do not disagree with God’s will. If, through ignorance, our will departs from God’s will, God’s good will corrects our foolish will, as happened to the apostle Paul. [Col. 0703D]

**VERSE 15.**—“We know that,” etc. Since we know that we have from him the petitions we ask, let us ask nothing opposed to him, nothing except what he has taught us and inspired us to ask; and if we err in anything, we are immediately corrected.

**VERSE 16.**—“Whoever knows his brother.” (Bede.) He is speaking of daily and minor sins, etc., up to the point where he says that you should chastise yourself for examination of those sins. [Col. 0704A]

“There is sin leading to death.” This sin separates one from God, just as death separates the soul from the body.

**VERSE 17.**—“Every iniquity is sin.” As though he said: One must indeed pray for those who sin without sinning unto death, because everyone is burdened by many sins, and no one can be without sin, since every iniquity is sin. Yet above and beyond these there is sin unto death, which is not committed through human frailty and therefore is not cleansed by the prayer of the righteous; for those who commit such things will not obtain the kingdom of God.

**VERSE 18.**—“Everyone who has been born,” etc. Whoever has been born of God does not sin unto death; whoever has not been born sins. But we are among those who have been born of God; therefore we will not sin and will not be touched by the enemy. Lovers of the world, however, are subject to the evil enemy. [Col. 0704B]

“He does not sin.” David sinned gravely, but because, having been born of God, he belonged to the fellowship of God’s sons, he did not sin unto death; rather, through repentance, he obtained forgiveness. “But the generation of God,” etc. Those who persevere in God’s generation cannot sin, nor can they be touched by the evil one. Just as day and night cannot be mingled, so neither can righteousness and iniquity, the evil one and the generation of God. The evil one therefore touches some, injuring and afflicting them, but not for their harm.

**VERSE 19.**—“And the whole world.” Not only lovers of the world, but also those newly born who have no discernment between good and evil, belong, because of the first transgression, to the kingdom of the devil unless they are rescued from darkness by God’s grace. [Col. 0704C]

**VERSE 20.**—“And we know,” etc. No one can attain eternal life without divine knowledge, and no one can know without God’s grace, because no one knows the Son except the Father, nor does anyone know the Father except the Son and the one to whom the Son wills to reveal both the Father and the Son. For the Son reveals both: appearing visibly in the flesh, he disclosed the mysteries of his divinity to the world through the Gospel.

**VERSE 21.**—“Little children.” Since you know the true God and true man, and await eternal life, guard yourselves from the doctrines of heretics. They assume an appearance of holiness and, through perverse doctrines, exchange the glory of the incorruptible God for the likeness of corruptible things. For avarice is the service of idols; therefore those who place the world before God are idolaters. [Col. 0704D]

“Guard yourselves.” Although he had borne witness to their perfection in many respects, it could nevertheless still be feared that someone newly converted might retain remnants of superstition in his mind. Therefore he shows that one must flee the worship of idols.

# THE SECOND EPISTLE OF BLESSED JOHN (G)*

## ARGUMENT

He writes to a holy woman so respectfully that he does not hesitate to address her as “lady” in his letter, and he bears witness concerning her children that they walk in the truth. [Col. 0703D]

## CHAPTER ONE

**VERSE 1.**—“Not I.” Since he is about to write against heretics who have fallen away from the truth, he says that all who know the truth have one love for the saints, so that, by the similarity of Catholics, he may deter them from the company of heretics. For all the faithful agree in one truth, whereas heretics attack one another in their errors. [Col. 0705A]

**VERSE 4.**—“I rejoiced greatly.” As though he said: What you hold, hold fast. Receive nothing else from the heretics, because I rejoice in what you have; I do not desire anything else to be added to you for salvation. Since, then, I rejoice in your good beginning, do not make me grieve at your failure, for, as a vigilant guardian, I know everything that happens among you.

“Walking in the truth.” Adam was placed in paradise to work it and guard it. Work signifies the advancement produced by action; guarding signifies the state and constancy of perfection itself. [Col. 0705B]

**VERSE 8.**—“Look to yourselves,” etc. Do not consent to such men; rather, take care that you are perfectly instructed in faith and steadfastness. But do this so that you may receive a full reward—that is, so that you may receive the true God with complete joy—by persevering in the doctrine handed down to you and not consenting to their error.

**VERSE 9.**—“And does not remain.” If anyone separates himself from divine doctrine, so that he is outside the right faith and the practice of God’s commandments, he separates himself from God, so that he does not have God. Through the active and contemplative life, God is manifested to someone by revealing himself as the Creator of all things. [Col. 0706A]

“Whoever remains.” He remains in evangelical doctrine who thinks and acts according to it; the one who thinks and acts otherwise separates himself from it.

**VERSE 10.**—“Do not say ‘Hail’ to him.” Since this appears to be a sign of agreement with error—for we say this to friends whose works please us—and even if you yourselves had not been deceived, others might nevertheless be deceived through such familiarity with you, believing that those people pleased you and therefore believing them.

**VERSE 12.**—“Having more to say.” Understand that this admonition will be very useful to you, because, to confirm it, I have also decided to come to you; yet meanwhile I could not remain entirely silent. [Col. 0706B]

**VERSE 13.**—“They greet you.” Just as he forbids the adversaries of truth to be greeted with “Hail,” so conversely he greets the elect in the person of the elect.

# THE THIRD EPISTLE OF BLESSED JOHN (G)*

## ARGUMENT

He praises Gaius because of his piety and exhorts him to remain in that piety. He rebukes Diotrephes because of his impiety and pride. He bears good witness to Demetrius together with all the brothers. [Col. 0705]

## CHAPTER ONE

**VERSE 2.**—“I pray concerning all things,” etc. Just as right intention now abounds in you, together with the continuing good will to give generously to the needy and the means of wealth, so may you always, with the Lord’s help, lead a life full of virtues. [Col. 0705C]

**VERSE 4.**—“I have no greater joy than these things.” I rejoiced for this reason: I have no greater joy concerning these brothers who come to me than when they announce that my children—whom I have begotten by preaching and baptizing—observe the truth of right faith and conduct.

**VERSE 5.**—“Beloved, you act faithfully,” etc. For this reason you must not cease from hospitality and almsgiving. Whatever you do faithfully for the brothers—that is, as a faithful person, as is fitting for one who is faithful—you do not do for empty glory, but you display your faith through your works. [Col. 0705D]

**VERSE 7.**—“For they have gone out for the sake of his name,” etc. As though he said: They truly deserve honor. They were not expelled from their homeland because of their crimes; rather, they departed voluntarily for the sake of advancing Christ’s name and suffering for his name.

**VERSE 9.**—“I might have written,” etc. You must persevere in almsgiving, because I understand that it is so beneficial that I would have written not only to you but also to the whole Church in commendation of almsgiving. But I abandoned this plan because of the necessity imposed by Diotrephes, who does not respect our authority. Diotrephes, a heresiarch of that time, was usurping primacy by teaching new doctrines. Diotrephes is interpreted as “handsomely foolish” or “beauty gone mad,” so that the name itself also marks the perfidy of his heart. [Col. 0706B]

“Of the Church.” I would have written to that Church which perhaps—this being stated doubtfully—is a Church, so that through the observance of almsgiving it might deserve to become a perfect Church. [Col. 0706C]

**VERSE 10.**—“I will bring it to light.” That is, by reproving him, I will bring him more openly before everyone’s knowledge. He has no example of these things anywhere, but does them and invents new ones, chattering and using false arguments to refute us and thus draw you away from the faith. Just as we must not stir up the tongues of detractors by our fault, lest they themselves perish, so we must bear patiently those tongues stirred up by their own malice, so that our merit may increase. At times, however, we must restrain them, lest, while they spread reports about us, they corrupt the hearts of those who could have heard what is good.

**VERSE 12.**—“Demetrius has testimony.” He makes clear that he wishes him to imitate the good, so that he may imitate Demetrius and himself become worthy of the similar praise of all. [Col. 0706D]

**VERSE 14.**—“Peace to you.” He conveys to his friends the grace of peace and salvation, so as to show that the enemies of truth are strangers to salvation.

# THE CATHOLIC EPISTLE OF JUDE (G)*

## ARGUMENT

The apostle Jude instructs the brothers concerning those who corrupt the way of truth, declaring that it is unlawful for those once freed from under the yoke of servitude to devote themselves again to servile obligations. [Col. 0705D]

## CHAPTER ONE

**VERSE 1.**—“Consoled and called.” Jesus our Lord calls, preserves, loves his children, and makes them members of God. [Col. 0707A]

**VERSE 2.**—“Mercy to you.” If God has begun to show you mercy by forgiving your sins, may he complete that mercy by leading you through abundant blessings to eternal things. If he has been reconciled to his enemies, may he grant eternal peace to those made his friends, in which you may disagree with him in nothing.

**VERSE 3.**—“Beloved.” I, who wish to care for your salvation, found it necessary, because of the false teachers who thrust themselves upon you, to write to you admonitions concerning your common salvation—that is, concerning the faith which is my salvation as much as yours and that of all the faithful, namely, the faith that works through love. I say that I am making every effort to write to you—that is, everything required of one who is solicitous. I pray for you; I argue against your seducers; and, so that you may know that I care for you, I write to you about them. I expose their wickedness; I show you how you must hold to faith and love; and since I am so solicitous for you, you ought to receive my admonition. [Col. 0707B]

**VERSE 4.**—“Transferring grace.” The harshness and strictness of the Law—which says, “An eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth”—are tempered by the grace of the Gospel, in which sins already committed are cleansed through repentance and the fruits of almsgiving. But the wicked transfer this grace into indulgence, and now sin all the more freely because they see themselves less rigorously examined for their crimes under the severity of the Law. [Col. 0707C]

**VERSE 5.**—“All things.” The mysteries of faith; you have no need to hear from new teachers anything recent as though it were holier. That is: You know perfectly everything about the faith that ought to be known, and therefore you have no need to listen to them.

“For Jesus.” Having refuted the heretics, he then recalls those who had believed the wicked and ungodly, showing how great is the Lord whom they deny and demonstrating that he is the one who led the people of Israel out of Egypt.

**VERSE 6.**—“But the angels.” Truly, those who falsely claim that Jesus is not true God but a man born from both sexes are not to be imitated. If he did not spare the angels who sinned, neither will he spare arrogant human beings.

“They did not keep their own principality.” So also human beings do not preserve the principality by which, through the grace of adoption, they were made sons of God. Instead, they abandon their dwelling—that is, the unity of the Church in which they were reborn—or the seats of the heavenly kingdom that they were to receive if they preserved the faith. Before the judgment he will condemn them severely, and even more severely in the universal judgment. [Col. 0707D]

“With eternal chains.” That is, with pride and an unrepentant heart; or with the divine sentence that will confine them forever; or the chain is the desire for lower things, by which they are bound and cannot return to higher things.

**VERSE 7.**—“As Sodom.” After giving an example of the condemnation of those who deny the one ruler, by recalling the destruction of the faithless people and of the angels who rose up against God, he also gives an example of the punishment of those who transfer the Lord’s grace into indulgence, recalling the burning of Sodom. [Col. 0708A]

**VERSE 8.**—“But they despise dominion.” In lesser sins, by blaspheming majesty; in criminal sins, by refusing humbly to confess and repent; having no fear and no faith in the coming judge.

**VERSE 9.**—“When Michael,” etc. That is, when Moses, who had been appointed as God to Pharaoh and who, in relation to the others, was prince and messenger, disputed with Pharaoh—namely, performed alternating signs against the signs of the magicians—concerning the body of Moses, that is, the people of Israel, so that he might allow them to sacrifice to their God, he did not dare to inflict the punishment of blasphemy in this world, but said: “May the Lord command you.”

Or otherwise: when the Lord Jesus disputed with Pilate concerning the body of Moses, that is, the Church, he did not wish to inflict any blasphemy, but was led like a sheep to the slaughter. [Col. 0708B]

**VERSE 11.**—“Woe to them,” etc. Since it has been shown that the heretics have fallen in every respect from the word of truth, he demonstrates that they are subject to various evils.

(Bede.) They go in the way of Cain because of envy, etc., up to the point where he says that they attack the truth they have known.

**VERSE 12.**—“Stains.” They do not perish and become stained only in carnal feasting and drunkenness; they themselves are also stains, and they destroy others with themselves by transferring the Lord’s grace into indulgence.

“Clouds.” They compare themselves with preachers who rain down righteousness and flash through miracles. But heretics are clouds that obscure the sun, setting their mouth in heaven by teaching perverse things arrogantly, without the water of wisdom. [Col. 0708C]

“But trees.” The wicked and false apostles compare themselves to trees bearing good fruit, but they are autumn trees. For they bear good fruit late, like a tree planted in autumn; or because at that time the leaves and fruit fall; or, if fruit grows upon them, it is counterfeit and useless. For if the wicked do anything that appears good, they do it not with a good intention, but so that they may uproot the good things existing in others.

“Twice dead.” (Bede.) One who bears no fruit dies once, etc., up to the point where he says “in which the saints are said to be rooted.”

**VERSE 13.**—“Stars.” By this he signifies apostates, because, in imitation of the devil, they fell from the seats of the angels, for whom darkness is reserved because of their apostasy. [Col. 0708D]

“Stars.” They promise the light of truth in this sea of vices, but they never persevere in the same condition of teaching or of life; they cause shipwreck for others, and for themselves, because of the darkness they introduced into the Church of God, the darkness of hell is prepared. Those who disturbed the peace of the faith with worldly tempest will be battered by a storm of torments.

**VERSE 14.**—“He prophesied.” He says: I do not prove by my authority alone that they are to be punished; I also prove it by the authority of Enoch, since long ago ungodly people were designated for such a judgment—people who in our times have secretly entered in to overthrow the faith of the godly.

“Enoch.” In the line of Cain, Enoch, whose name means “dedication,” is born first; in the lineage of the elect, Enoch is remembered as the seventh. The reprobate dedicate themselves in this present life, which comes first, by building themselves up; but the elect await the dedication of their building at the end of time, that is, in the seventh age. [Col. 0709A]

“Behold, the Lord comes.” (Bede.) It is a true judgment that the Lord will rebuke the ungodly and concerning their works, etc., up to the point where he says that it is permissible to take testimony to the truth even from apocryphal writings.

**VERSE 16.**—“These are they.” If anything good happens to the brothers, they murmur and complain, as though their own happiness were diminished by the prosperity of others. For the avaricious—who are satisfied by nothing—also envy what belongs to others.

**VERSE 19.**—“Not having the Spirit.” Because they do not have the Holy Spirit, through whom the spiritual Church is gathered and made spiritual, they are therefore animal, ignorant, and unproviding. Thus they drift away, because they do not possess the bond of charity. [Col. 0709B]

**VERSE 20.**—“Building yourselves up,” etc. Build yourselves up in good works upon the foundation of faith, so that you may be placed as living stones in the house of God.

“Praying in the Holy Spirit.” Do not presume upon your own strength, but hope in the help of divine protection. Do not think that you can be saved by yourselves; rather, ask for the coming of the Holy Spirit into you, so that, inspired by him, you may pray more fervently and not be separated from the Church together with those who do not possess the Spirit. [Col. 0710A]

**VERSE 23.**—“But save them.” Teach those who are not condemned before God but are even close to falling into the fire to free themselves.

“In fear.” (Bede.) This must be joined to all the preceding matters. For, etc., up to the point where he says that one should be careful lest he prove more severe or more merciful than is right.

“Hating even the garment.” We must not hate our body, but hate it as stained, so that we may restore it unstained, so that what is carnal may become spiritual. This is to be accomplished not by the power of our own will but by God’s grace.

**VERSE 21.**—“In exultation.” Those whom he earlier warned to serve God in fear he says should be established in exultation, because the more fearful we are now concerning our actions, the more greatly we shall rejoice in the future over the reward we have received. [Col. 0710B]

**VERSE 25.**—“Glory and magnificence.” If you possess the glory of pure faith and conscience, magnificence in action, authority over weakness or over demons, and power to resist vices or torturers, attribute these things to God, not to yourselves. He is glorious in his essence before all ages, in the present, and after all ages; magnificent in his works; ruling both those who willingly obey and those who do not; and powerful, with nothing able to resist him.

# THE APOCALYPSE OF BLESSED JOHN (G)*

## JEROME’S PROLOGUE

John the apostle and evangelist, chosen and beloved by Christ, was held in such abundant affection that at the supper he reclined upon Christ’s breast, and, standing alone at the cross, received Christ’s own mother into his care. Thus, to the one whom he had called, when he wished to marry, to embrace virginity, he also entrusted for safekeeping the Virgin. [Col. 0709C]

When, therefore, on account of the word of God and the testimony of Jesus Christ, John was assigned exile on the island of Patmos, the Apocalypse was there shown beforehand by Christ and written down, so that, just as at the beginning of the canon, that is, in the book of Genesis, an incorruptible beginning is marked out, so also an incorruptible end might be given through the virgin in the Apocalypse, which says: “I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end.” [Col. 0709D]

This is John who, knowing that the day of his departure from the body had come upon him, summoned his disciples in Ephesus, descended into the excavated place of his burial, and, when his prayer was complete, gave up his spirit. He was as much a stranger to the pain of death as he is known to have been free from the corruption of the flesh. The arrangement of this Scripture, or the organization of the book, is not expounded by us piece by piece for this reason: that the ignorant may acquire a desire to inquire, those who inquire the fruit of labor, and the teaching office may be reserved for God.

## ARGUMENT

The Apocalypse of John contains as many mysteries as it has words. I have said too little, and every praise is inferior to the worth of the book. In each individual word, multiple meanings lie hidden. [Col. 0710C]

## CHAPTER ONE

**VERSE 1.**—“The Apocalypse of Jesus Christ.” He prepares his hearers and makes them favorable and attentive, as also there: “John to the seven churches that are in Asia.”

“Which he gave.” According to his humanity, Christ receives it from the Father, from the Word hypostatically joined to him, and from the Holy Spirit.

“Which must take place.” As though he said: It is inevitable that these things happen, and it is beneficial that they happen. It is necessary that servants soon suffer tribulations.

“Soon.” He says “soon” so that they may prepare themselves and not find suffering burdensome. Their labors must soon end, and rewards must be given. Brief is the labor; hastened is the glory. [Col. 0710D]

**VERSE 2.**—“Who bore witness.” He testifies that the words themselves of Christ are true, words concerning both the Word—that is, the divinity—and the humanity of Jesus Christ.

“The Word of God.” The Son is called the Word of God because through him the Father was manifested in the world.

“In the things that he saw.” In the things he saw bodily, such as Christ suffering and dying, and in the things he saw only with the mind, such as Christ’s having been with the Father before all things.

**VERSE 3.**—“Blessed.” Christ gave these things to me, but blessed is the one who has received me. Blessed because this Apocalypse is of Jesus Christ, etc.

“Who reads.” That is, who recounts to others what he has heard, since many can hear from one person reading; or, “those who hear,” and in this he indicates the hearers, because they are many. Those alone are blessed who hear in order to store the words in their minds; who store them in their minds in order to fulfill them in action; and who fulfill them in action in order to possess eternal life. [Col. 0711A]

“Who keeps them.” For it is not hearers of the Law but doers who are righteous. He keeps them who does not violate the faith of Christ and the Church, fears the things threatened, and seeks the things promised. Such a person is truly blessed, because the labor does not last long and the rewards are near.

**VERSE 4.**—“To the seven churches.” He writes principally to those churches of Asia over which he had been appointed teacher, and through their likeness to the others; or, through the seven, to the universal Church. For seven signifies totality, or because they are enlightened by the sevenfold Spirit.

“In Asia.” Asia means “elevation.” Therefore the Church is now in the elevation of virtues, or formerly in that of vices. This Asia is not that great third part of the world, but a certain province in which there were seven cities and seven churches with seven bishops. [Col. 0711B]

“Grace to you.” In his greeting he prepares his hearers and makes them favorable and attentive, as in the prologue.

“Who is and who was.” Eternally. Although he was born in time, he is already immutable in his humanity, though formerly corruptible. He will come in such a form, even if he does not appear such to the world.

“And from the seven spirits who are before his sight.” “Spirit” has the same meaning as “charity.” Hence forgiveness of sins and the other gifts, which are gifts of the whole Trinity, are attributed to the Spirit, so that we may understand that the Trinity acts solely through love. He passes over the person of the Father in silence because no one had understood evil concerning God the Creator; he mentions the person of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, concerning whom all the heresies arise in the churches.

“Thrones.” The thrones of God are his angels and holy human beings, in whom God now sits and judges, so that he need not judge in the future. [Col. 0711C]

**VERSE 5.**—“The faithful witness.” He says this because of those who despair concerning Christ’s death, such as those who said, “We had hoped that he was the one who would redeem Israel” (Luke 24).

“Firstborn of the dead.” As though he said: Let this not terrify you, because he rose and is impassible. Or he is the first of those who put themselves to death, because he committed no sin.

“Ruler of the kings of the earth.” He is ruler of earthly powers, able to remove them and permitting the wicked to serve for the benefit of his own people or of the saints.

**VERSE 6.**—“And he made us a kingdom for our God.” That is, powerful to resist vices, and priests—that is, offering ourselves to God for ourselves and for our brothers.

**VERSE 7.**—“Behold, he comes,” etc. You ought indeed to glorify him, because he is the one who will come to give rewards. [Col. 0711D]

“With the clouds,” that is, with the saints, because the clouds rained doctrine upon others and performed miracles; or, just as he ascended in a cloud, so he will come in a cloud. By this we understand the mercy of God, which is refreshment and illumination to the good but terror and blindness to the wicked. This was also signified by the cloud in which the children of Israel were led out of Egypt.

“And every eye will see him.” Another translation has: “Every land will see one such as this.” As though he said: They will see him as the one whom the wicked did not believe would come.

“Every eye.” The good will see him so as to rejoice; the wicked, so as to be confounded.

“They will mourn.” Or they will strike themselves against him, powerless to resist his authority, like a stone and earthen vessels; or they will mourn for themselves, that is, grieve when they see those who are founded upon him, because they will grieve not so much over the torment itself as over being rejected from such fellowship. [Col. 0712A]

**VERSE 8.**—“I am.” He will truly come, because he himself promises that he will come. Or, having given the greeting above, he makes them attentive, as though he said: Do not believe that this was spoken by me; believe that it was spoken by Christ himself.

“Alpha, the beginning.” Before him there was no one, or from him all things began.

“Omega, the end.” After him there will be no one, or in him all things will come to an end.

**VERSE 9.**—“I, John.” Having completed the greeting, he proceeds to the narrative by setting forth four elements—the person, the place, the reason for the place, and the time—which serve to commend the revelation itself. [Col. 0712B]

“I, John.” As though he said: I know that you are suffering, but suffer patiently by Christ’s example, so that you may share in his kingdom.

“Your brother,” etc., “in Christ.” In the unity of faith, and I was afflicted because of that faith, as were others. Through this I patiently endured in order to reach the kingdom, having Christ as an example in all things.

“Patmos.” That is, a strait, namely, tribulation, in which heavenly things are disclosed more fully to the faithful. The Church is compared to an island, because just as an island is battered by sea storms, so the Church is afflicted by the persecutions of those of the sea—that is, of worldly people.

“Because of the word of God.” That is, because of the testimony given to his divinity and humanity.

**VERSE 10.**—“On the Lord’s day.” The nature of events is often marked by the time, as when Abraham saw the angel in the heat of faith at midday; Lot, at evening, saw the destruction of Sodom; Adam heard the voice of the Lord after midday; and Solomon, not intending to keep wisdom in reserve, received wisdom at night. [Col. 0712C]

“I heard behind me a voice.” He heard it behind him because, while being led away from present things and stretching himself toward the things ahead in true contemplation, he was also admonished to look back upon others; or he hears it behind him because this had been foretold by the Law and the Prophets—that is what he understands.

**VERSE 11.**—“Write what you see.” A general admonition is given to John, instructing him generally to send it to the churches of Asia, through which all the other churches are to be understood. This general admonition extends to the words, “And to the angel of Ephesus,” etc. Whether John saw this vision all at once and in a single view, or at different times, the angel could have conveyed it to him in either manner.

“Ephesus.” Ephesus is interpreted as “my will,” or “a deep fall,” or “counsel.” [Col. 0712D]

**VERSE 12.**—“And I turned.” Because I heard the voice, I turned, etc.

“Seven lampstands.” That is, seven churches burning and illuminated by the wisdom of the divine Word.

“Golden.” Just as gold tested by fire and extended by blows becomes a lampstand, so the Church, purified by tribulations and stretched through the blows of temptations into long-suffering, is brought to perfection. If it has a voice in its mouth but not in its works, it is indeed a lampstand, but it is not golden.

**VERSE 13.**—“Like a son of man.” That is, an angel in the person of Christ. He is no longer called “the Son of Man,” but “like” the Son of Man, because he no longer dies. Or, Christ appeared like the Son of Man because he appeared not with sin but in the likeness of sinful flesh, in whom are all things necessary for governing the Church. [Col. 0713A]

“Clothed in a priestly robe.” That is, in the priestly garment, namely, the flesh in which he offered himself and daily offers himself, presenting himself to God the Father. Or the priestly robe is the Church, with which God is clothed like a tunic. It is called “reaching to the feet” because the Church will endure until the end of the world.

“Girded about the breasts.” Daniel saw him girded about the loins in the Old Testament, because carnal things are restrained there; here we read that he is girded about the breasts, because in the New Testament even thoughts are judged.

**VERSE 14.**—“His hairs were white.” That is, the saints, made thin and clinging to the head itself. Or, his thoughts. [Col. 0713B]

“Like wool.” Just as white wool is suited to receive any colors, so the saints are suited to endure tribulations.

“Like snow.” Snow is the whiteness of immortality, because it is whiter than every creature.

“His eyes.” That is, the gifts of the Holy Spirit. These belong to Christ as the one who possesses and gives them, and to the Church as the one who receives them; they enlighten and make one burn. Or the eyes are the spiritual people themselves in the Church, or the divine commandments.

**VERSE 15.**—“And his feet.” That is, the last faithful, who through many shakings will not retain their former nature, like brass, which is repeatedly heated and takes on a better color.

“In a burning furnace.” Another translation has: “Like Lebanese brass,” by which it is shown that in that region where the Lord was crucified this tribulation will have particular force.

“And his voice was like the voice of many waters.” That is, his preaching possesses the power of water because it cleanses. Or because many peoples have already received this voice—peoples compared to water because of their flowing movement—you ought all the more to stand firm. Or it is a voice giving many waters, that is, graces; hence what follows immediately: [Col. 0713C]

**VERSE 16.**—“Stars.” The stars are bishops, who ought to shine upon others through the word and the example of their lives. Even if they sin, they are called stars according to what they were established to be. He holds them in his right hand—that is, in the more excellent gifts signified by the right hand.

“And from his mouth.” That is, through God’s inspiration preaching went forth. It cuts both ways: in the Old Testament, carnal works; in the New, desires. Therefore it is written concerning this sword, which is the word of God: “For it is not you who speak, but the Spirit of your Father who speaks in you.” [Col. 0713D]

“Like the sun shines in strength.” That is, at midday without clouds; or as Christ himself in the resurrection; or when he will be fixed forever.

### Verse 17

**“I fell.”** That is, I cast off the care of humanity, in the likeness of the last faithful. **“Like a dead man.”** Dead to the world, alive to God, and desiring nothing earthly. **“His right hand.”** Namely, the Holy Spirit who strengthens, that is, his help. **“Do not fear.”** Fear not to suffer tribulations and death for me, because I—who had no need of this on my own account, since I am the first and the last—was dead and am alive.

### Verse 18

**“I am the living one.”** And therefore do not be terrified, because I clearly rose again and will not die anymore. **“And I have…”** And therefore I will not allow you to be tempted beyond what you can bear, because I have power over the devil and over his members. **“Of death and of hell.”** The devil is death, because he is the cause of sin, that is, of death; his ministers are hell, in whom he has his place.

### Verse 19

**“The things that must take place after this.”** In the last faithful, through whose example these others ought to be greatly encouraged.

### Verse 20

**“The mystery.”** That is, the hidden meaning, where one thing is seen and another is understood. This first vision concerns the correction of the churches. The angel partly discloses the allegory, so that he may teach that it must be sought everywhere.

## Chapter II

### Verse 1

**“And to the angel…”** That is, he writes to the bishop, from whose hand the sins of his subjects will be required, and without whose consent John himself does not presume to judge the subjects.

**“Of the church at Ephesus.”** Ephesus is interpreted, according to the portion of those who persevere in goodness, as “will,” because God delights in their works. He proposes these things so that they may be corrected through the example of those who had fallen. Ephesus is also interpreted as “counsel,” that is, “in need of counsel”; or as “a deep fall,” or “my will.”

**“Seven.”** He begins particular admonitions, each of which can also be universal, according to the different members of any church.

**“You cannot endure.”** By the force of humanity. Or: “You cannot endure them without correcting or expelling them.”

### Verse 2

**“You tested those who call themselves…”** Only those who are inside the Church are tested.

### Verse 3

**“You endured for the sake of my name.”** You did not do this for human praise, but for the glorification of my name.
