**“And you have not grown weary.”** He indicates that human weakness would have been the cause of failure, unless help had come beforehand.

### Verse 4

**“But I have this against you: that you have abandoned charity.”** Either the bishop, in his own person, is reproved for becoming weary of the vices found among his subjects; or the subjects are found to sin through love of earthly things. Eli the priest was good, and yet he was condemned because he was unwilling to correct his sons.

### Verse 5

**“I will move your lampstand.”** I will take away the virtues and gifts of the Holy Spirit through which the lampstands have been established.

### Verse 6

**“But you have this good quality.”** Although this is against you, nevertheless do not despair, because you possess something good.

**“The deeds of the Nicolaitans.”** That is, the common use of women and the eating of things sacrificed to idols.

[Col. 0714D]

### Verse 7

**“Whoever has an ear…”** Why must he listen? Because, for the one who perseveres, Christ is the tree of life: a shelter, a source of strength, and one who gives fruit, that is, his body and blood, both here and especially in the future.

### Verse 8

**“Of Smyrna.”** Smyrna is interpreted as “song,” or as something like myrrh. A song is something in which people take delight; myrrh is so bitter that it even preserves bodies from decay.

**“Thus says the first.”** He describes Christ in such a way as to provide consolation to those upon whom tribulations are inflicted.

**“Thus says the first.”** It is as though he said: “Do not fail, because I, so great, suffered death for you, and from it I rose again. Expect the same yourselves.”

### Verse 10

**“Some of you.”** Here it is clear that this is understood not of one alone but of several.

**“So that you may be tested.”** That is, so that you may be proved, or so that you may be despised by the devil and his members.

**“For ten days.”** That is, during the time of that warfare. For when God sends his own into battle, he arms them with the Decalogue. Or, “for ten days” means throughout the whole period in which, over seven days, one fights against the three principal vices: avarice, desire, and vainglory.

### Verse 11

**“From the second death.”** The first death of the soul is in sins, the second in punishments. The first death of the body occurs when it is dissolved; the second when it is condemned at the judgment.

### Verse 12

**“The sword”—*rhomphaea*.** He requires these people to possess this sword in the choosing of good and the rejection of evil.

### Verse 13

**“You did not deny my faith.”** Tribulation is illumination for the righteous, correction for the obstinate, and blindness for the hardened.

### Verse 14

**“Balaam.”** By Balaam are understood heretics who teach earthly rulers how to overthrow the worshipers of the true God. Or Balaam means demons, who teach the flesh to deceive souls that behold God.

### Verse 15

**“The teaching of the Nicolaitans.”** He repeats what he said about the Nicolaitans in order to invite them to repentance, which he did not do.

### Verse 17

**“Manna.”** By manna understand eternal glory, concerning which all will say, “What is this?” For “eye has not seen, nor ear heard” (1 Cor. II), and so forth.

**“And I will give him…”** It is written in Daniel: “A stone was cut out without hands” (Dan. I). In Proverbs: “A very precious jewel is the expectation of one who waits” (Prov. XVII). This likewise signifies the solid body, luminous in itself, white with virtues and with the hope of immortality.

**“And on the stone.”** Or: upon baptism add martyrdom, whose force the hypocrite does not understand when he suffers for human praise.

**“Written.”** In five letters, namely, the five wounds with which his body was displayed on the cross, showing that he was a martyr.

### Verse 19

**“I know your works,”** and so forth. The Son possesses the gifts of the Holy Spirit—that is, he gives them to whom he wills, or takes them away. Therefore let those who have already received these gifts beware lest they lose them through consenting to evil.

Or understand this as charity and faith, with the order reversed—for charity does not come before faith. First comes faith; from faith, charity; from charity, good works.

### Verse 20

**“To fornicate.”** Fornication is said to be fourfold: in the mind—“If you look at a woman in order to desire her” (Matt. V), and so forth; in the act itself; in love of earthly things; and in the worship of idols.

### Verse 24

**“I will not cast upon you…”** Certain false Christians terrified them by saying that the Lord would still send greater tribulations than those they had suffered. Against this he says that he will not send them.

## Chapter III

### Verse 1

**“And to the angel of the church at Sardis.”** Sardis is interpreted as “the beginning of beauty.” By this is signified one who at first possesses no virtue, or little virtue, and afterward becomes ugly through vices. Or hypocrites are meant: beautiful outwardly, deformed within.

**“I know your works.”** And I know that in all your works you seek human praise.

[Col. 0716A]

### Verse 2

**“Be watchful.”** Watch, therefore, because although you are unmoved in mind, or praiseworthy in mind, you are nevertheless not perfect unless you stir up the others. It is not enough to confess Christ unless you also perform works.

**“For I have not found your works complete.”** This is because you are without charity, or act for the sake of praise, or commit a mortal crime.

### Verse 3

**“Keep in mind, therefore.”** That is, remember how you received the faith of Christ in baptism, where you promised that you would renounce the devil and all his pomps. Remember also that you heard from teachers of the Christian faith how you ought to live. Preserve what you heard, and do penance because you have remained sluggish in good works for so long.

You heard from the holy Fathers that “whoever offends in one point is guilty of all”; hence, “if I do not have charity, I am nothing” (James II).

[Col. 0716B]

### Verse 4

**“They have not defiled their garments.”** The garments of immortality and innocence that they received in baptism; or their good works.

### Verse 5

**“I will not erase…”** He erases the reprobate, according to the saying: “The Lord hardened Pharaoh’s heart” (Exod. X).

**“From the book of life.”** The book of life is the foreknowledge of God, in which all things are contained.

**“I will confess his name,”** saying: “Come, blessed of my Father” (Matt. XXV). Or here: “You gave me food and drink.”

### Verse 7

**“Thus says…”** It is as though he said: “Labor for the conversion of the brethren as you have begun, because in the promise I made—‘Whatever you ask the Father in my name, he will give you’ (John XIV)—I am truthful in my promises. From this you can know that I will gather many to you, as you desire.”

**“He closes.”** He closes so that we may seek; he opens so that we may find, so that the seeker may receive the fruit of his labor and the giver may receive thanks for his goodness.

### Verse 8

**“Behold, I have set before you…”** I have rightly done so, because you could not openly possess it by yourself, since you have little strength.

**“A door.”** Through the door—which is so called from *obstando*, “resisting”—are understood the hearts of human beings, formerly hard. Or you may understand obscure Scriptures. Or Christ, who is the true door to life. Hence, when the disciples were forbidden to speak and were beaten, they said: “We cannot but speak of what we have seen” (Acts IV).

### Verse 9

**“Jews.”** They lost this name when they said of Christ, “We do not know this man” (John IX).

**“They are lying.”** They strive to establish their claim by words and by certain simulations.

**“Behold, I will make them come…”** They are prepared to imitate your works through a semblance of your humility.

**“They will know.”** Those outside did not believe that God loved the Church, which he allowed to be afflicted. But now he will make the evidence of his love manifest—that is, he will establish certainty—so that you do not succumb, because he is coming to reward you.

### Verse 10

**“You have kept the word of my patience.”** The command concerning patience that I displayed when praying for my persecutors.

**“From the hour of testing.”** Either the general persecution of Christians that was to occur immediately after Nero, or the final period of the Antichrist.

**“To test those who dwell on the earth.”** Just as in what follows, where the sixth order is mentioned repeatedly, so here in the sixth angel the final persecution is signified. In it, some of the Jews will be deceived; others, fulfilling the Law spiritually according to Elijah’s admonitions, will believe that they will conquer the enemy.

[Col. 0717A]

### Verse 11

**“Behold, I am coming soon.”** It is as though he said: “The testing will indeed come, but do not succumb, because I am coming to reward you.”

### Verse 12

**“A pillar in the temple.”** Firm in himself and sustaining others by word and example.

**“He will not go out.”** Since God has a fixed number of his own, if one falls, another is introduced in his place by his mercy, just as, through the pride of the Jews, the Gentiles entered in their place.

The younger son—that is, the Gentile people—had gone out; but, reconciled through the death of the fattened calf, that is, through Christ’s blood, he will not go out again.

**“New.”** Where there is nothing of antiquity, but a full vision of peace.

**“From heaven.”** From conformity with the heavenly creatures.

[Col. 0717B]

### Verse 14

**“A witness of what he heard from the Father, fearless.”** Or, one whose testimony must be accepted in all things. Or, a witness of our works before the Father.

**“And true.”** He is truth, because through him the Father’s promises are fulfilled.

### Verse 15

**“You are neither cold nor hot,”** because you neither entirely ignore the faith you have received nor openly deny it.

**“Would that you were cold.”** He does not simply wish him to be cold, but wishes him to be such a person concerning whom there might be greater hope.

### Verse 16

**“I will begin to vomit you out.”** He is about to say something remarkable: that the lukewarm are to be excommunicated because they were considered good by human beings. He says that he is truthful in all things so that he may be believed in this matter as well. If they wish to come to their senses, he promises their preservation, because he gave them the first faith.

**“From my mouth.”** One is vomited from the mouth when one is precipitated into worse things, or when one dies unrepentant.

### Verse 17

**“I am rich,”** either in divine knowledge or in secular knowledge.

### Verse 18

**“I advise you to buy from me gold refined by fire.”** For works of that sort will not lead to salvation.

**“So that your shame may not appear.”** It is better to blush here before a few than in the future before everyone.

**“Eye salve.”** Our eyes are anointed in order that we may see, when we assist the sharpness of our understanding with the medicine of good works so as to recognize the brightness of the true light: “The commandment of the Lord enlightens the eyes” (Ps. XVIII). Or: anoint the mind, which earthly things had enclosed, with the gift of the Holy Spirit.

### Verse 20

**“Behold, I stand at the door and knock.”** “If anyone hears,” and so forth. I wait, or inspire, or call through preachers.

### Verse 21

**“To sit with me on my throne.”** To judge in those in whom I sit and judge.

These things concern prelates and, through the prelates, their subjects.

**“Just as I conquered and sat with my Father on his throne.”** He says this because Christ’s victory and session are the cause of the Christians’ victory and session.

## Chapter IV

### Verse 1

**“After this I saw…”** In this second vision he treats of the one seated on the throne, of his adornment, and of the Lamb opening the book—that is, the divine plan for the restoration of the human race—and of the one who loosens the seven seals, that is, the obscurities. When we see that God has bestowed such great understanding of the Scriptures upon human beings, we should be grateful to him and not fear suffering for his sake.

**“In heaven.”** That is, in Scripture, which is the way to life. Or Christ is the door, whose mysteries, formerly closed, are now open to those who are heaven through faith and works.

**“Like a trumpet speaking with me.”** Not disagreeing with my rational understanding, but providing these explanations.

**“I will show you…”** After speaking of the things that have already passed, he also speaks of what must still happen, which will continue in the same condition in which they began. Or, after the correction, it is necessary to see the secrets by which they may be encouraged for battle. Or, “the things that must happen soon after this” means among the last faithful. Or, “after this I was in the Spirit.”

[Col. 0718B]

### Verse 2

**“Immediately I was…”** I did not resist, but cast off concern for all earthly things.

**“And behold, a throne…”** These are those in whom God sits and judges, and also the subjects, some of whom are so suitable that God may properly sit and rest in them.

**“The one seated.”** Above, Christ was said to walk among the lampstands; now he is seated, that is, judging the merits of each person. It is fitting that he is remembered here, since he exhorted them to battle.

### Verse 3

**“The one seated…”** Where all are good, there is no need to judge—that is, to distinguish. Where there are good and evil, discrimination is necessary.

**“He was like in appearance.”** Formerly unknown, he appeared to the world through the flesh, crushing enemies and granting strength to his own.

**“Of jasper and sardius.”** Through the color of the two stones, he signifies God and man.

**“Of emerald.”** Through the green color of the emerald, which is the color of water, baptism is understood. Through its redness, the gifts of the Holy Spirit received in baptism are signified, by which sins are burned away.

### Verse 4

**“Twenty-four elders.”** Twelve prophets and twelve apostles, although there are more in both orders.

**“Clothed all around in white robes.”** The sins of the righteous are covered, and they themselves are made white by virtues.

**“Crowns.”** That is, victory through wisdom and charity, even toward enemies.

### Verse 5

**“From the throne.”** That is, from the Church. That is, water rains lightning—namely, miracles that terrify and illuminate.

**“Seven spirits.”** The lamps are the gifts of the Holy Spirit, which kindle and illuminate, prepared for all those who are the seat of God.

[Col. 0718D]

### Verse 6

**“In the presence…”** Because they understand both the mystery and the reality of the mystery, and admit only those whom they see and know to be suitable.

**“A glassy sea.”** Baptism, bright with the sincerity of faith, after which the elect are led by the fire of tribulation toward firmness in good works, just as crystal hardens from water.

**“In the midst.”** He describes a certain level place appearing in the likeness of the great judge, who has a broad and spacious street where he sits and gives judgment.

**“Of the throne.”** By the name “throne” Jerusalem is understood; or supports are meant, represented by a man, a calf, a lion, and an eagle.

**“Four.”** Because of the office of fourfold preaching.

**“Living creatures.”** These properly represent Christ, who was born, suffered, rose again, and ascended.

The faithful also are rational and gentle, like a man; they trample adversities without fear, like a lion; they put themselves to death, like a calf; they seek heavenly things, like an eagle.

**“Full of eyes.”** They remember past sins and guard themselves against the future; or they possess knowledge of what God has done or will do at the end of the world; or they please God and human beings.

[Col. 0719A]

### Verse 7

**“A lion.”** A lion is born dead and is brought to life on the third day by its father’s voice. So Christ also rose on the third day. He had to rise because he had died; he had to die because he was human; and the dead man both wished and was able to rise because he was an eagle—that is, God.

### Verse 8

**“And the four living creatures, each of them, had six wings.”** This was so that they might preach these things about Christ, in which they had been well instructed.

**“Six wings.”** The first wing is the natural law; the second, the law of Moses; the third, the prophets; the fourth, the Gospel; the fifth, the institutions of the apostles; the sixth, the decrees of various authorities, such as Augustine, Gregory, and Ambrose, through whom the Church seeks higher things and from whom preachers receive the foundation of all preaching.

Or the six wings are knowledge of God’s works, made in six days. Those who work well in these things raise their knowledge on high.

**“Around and within.”** According to the letter, they instruct the simple; according to the allegory, they instruct the more perfect, and illuminate the middle and the ends of the earth.

**“They are full of eyes.”** Because they keep themselves pure and instruct others by their example. Or they are full of eyes within—that is, pure in conscience—and around them—that is, irreproachable in the sight of human beings.

**“Who is to come.”** The Son will appear bodily; the whole Godhead will manifest itself to the faithful in its own manner.

### Verse 9

**“And blessing,”** namely, the reward from above; or blessing in exaltation, so that every knee of those in heaven, on earth, and under the earth may bow to him (Phil. II).

### Verse 10

**“And they worshiped.”** They sought from him, in word and deed, what they did not possess from themselves.

**“Saying.”** In the secret of their hearts, they attributed to God the victory over vices and tribulations.

### Verse 11

**“You created all things.”** Therefore everything must be referred to you, because everything receives its beginning from you.

He also created invisible things, including angels and souls, so that he is said to create spiritual beings when he makes the impious spiritually pious.

**“By your will.”** And not suddenly. “And what was made, in him was life” (John I).

**“They were.”** In the mind, before they were formed in their works.

**“They were created.”** By coming into visible existence.

Therefore all things existed from eternity insofar as they were in the divine mind, but they began to exist in time through creation.

## Chapter V

### Verse 1

**“And I saw in the right hand of the one seated…”** By the right hand I understand the Son, through whom God the Father made all things, and toward whom the entire purpose of the book is directed.

**“A book.”** That is, the two Testaments, which are one and the same book.

**“On the outside.”** This signifies the Old Testament, which promises external things.

**“Within.”** This signifies the New Testament, which often and clearly promises blessedness.

**“Sealed.”** The writings of the prophets were made closed and obscure, but afterward they were opened through Christ.

[Col. 0720A]

**“With seals.”** That is, with all obscurities; or it was closed with the sevenfold Spirit, through whom faith is opened.

**“Seven.”** He says this because, as he will specify below, these are the seven seals: the white horse, the red horse, the black horse, and so forth. These were opened and made known at the beginning of the Church. The Church was the white horse upon which Christ sat, strengthening it by doctrine and example; the red horse attacked it.

### Verse 2

**“An angel.”** The holy and ancient fathers of the Old Testament sometimes understood that God had arranged the restoration of Jerusalem. They longed to see when it would take place, but they did not know how it would happen, until he revealed it to certain people before it occurred.

**“Proclaiming.”** Inquiring, announcing it to others, and, out of excessive longing, complaining that it had been delayed for so long.

**“To open the book.”** To disclose the divine plan and remove all the obscurities of the Scriptures.

### Verse 4

**“I wept greatly.”** This is spoken in the person of the earlier and ancient fathers, because they did not understand, or because they grieved over the delayed restoration. Hence: “Many kings and prophets desired to see…” (Luke X), and so forth.

### Verse 5

**“And one of the elders…”** Any prophet consoles others by announcing Christ’s coming.

**“The lion has conquered.”** When a lion is driven away, it flees through the mountains and erases its tracks with the knot at the end of its tail, so that it may not be found. Thus Christ fled through the mountains: that is, his divinity was hidden from the Jews; having assumed flesh, he concealed his divinity so that he could not be recognized.

A lion sleeps with its eyes open; so Christ expired while his divinity remained alive.

[Col. 0720C]

### Verse 6

**“And behold, in the midst of the throne…”** The Church, which Christ possesses as a throne, which is fed like the living creatures, and which is honored like the elders in the authority of judgment, is itself built upon Christ. It is exalted in a kingdom through the seven horns of strength and illuminated in the seven eyes by signs and virtues.

**“Like one slain.”** Although he died, he nevertheless lives by the power of God. Or he is like one slain among his own, in whom he is put to death daily.

**“Seven horns,”** and so forth. This is because he gives the kingdom, which is signified by the horns.

**“Eyes,”** because he illuminates.

Or the horns are the more eminent saints, founded upon Christ the head, who surpass the flesh.

### Verse 8

**“They fell before the Lamb.”** They held humble thoughts about themselves, imitating him; hence what follows:

**“Each holding a harp.”** The mortifications of vices and desires. In a harp there are wood and strings: through the wood, Christ’s cross is signified; through the strings, the flesh of the saints, which is stretched upon the wood. By returning the same sound through various torments, they imitate Christ’s cross.

### Verse 9

**“They sang a song.”** With exultation, the Church professes the New Testament through its works, when it baptizes into his death.

**“Tribe.”** The word is derived from three orders. In each order there are seventy-two languages; from these come many peoples, and within the people, nations.

The three orders of those to be saved are Noah, Daniel, and Job. Or the three orders of the nations are Greeks, Hebrews, and Christians.

### Verse 11

**“I saw.”** Not only did I see the living creatures and elders, who bore the same testimony according to their office, but I also heard—

[Col. 0721A]

**“The voice of angels.”** That is, of the heavenly spirits who strengthen and protect the Church, who rejoice over the restoration of the fellowship of the saints, and who bear witness to Christ: at his birth, when they appeared to the shepherds; at his passion; at his resurrection; and at his ascension, they testified that the judge would come.

Or the angels are the lesser subjects within the Church, living an angelic life. They surround and honor their preachers and judges, agreeing with and conforming themselves to their testimony.

**“Many around the throne, the living creatures, and the elders,”** and so forth. The more numerous they are, the greater the testimony and the greater the joy.

**“Thousands of thousands.”** He uses this number because what is infinite to human beings is finite with God.

### Verse 12

**“Wisdom and strength,”** and so forth. The knowledge of all things, as the Word united to him possesses it.

[Col. 0721B]

### Verse 13

**“Blessing.”** That is, the increase that we possess in good works; the honor that follows from them; the glory arising from the virtues we receive in baptism; and the power by which we resist desires—all these should be attributed not to us but to you.

### Verse 14

**“And the four living creatures.”** All the elders and living creatures assent to the testimony of the angels.

**“They fell upon their faces,”** and so forth. They do not grow proud because they judge others, but humble themselves.

## Chapter VI

### Verse 1

**“And I saw.”** After the Lamb had fulfilled what had been foretold concerning him and had established his Church in faith through the testimony of the prophets and angels, he opened their understanding so that they might understand the Scriptures. Through preachers he declares outwardly that it is fitting to suffer for this faith and what aids or crowns he offers to his own.

Since he had recalled the restoration, if he remained silent about tribulations they might already fail if tribulation arose unexpectedly.

**“When he had opened…”** This book was sealed because Christ opened everything either in himself or in his own. He opened their understanding so that they might understand these seals in the Scriptures.

In the first seal, when the white horse went out, the Church’s whitening through baptism is understood. In the second, the red horse signifies the manifest persecution of those who shed blood, from which tribulations rise against the baptized. In the third, the black horse signifies the hidden persecution of heretics. In the fourth, the pale horse signifies the manifest and hidden persecution arising from false accusations.

**“Come and see.”** Pass from the mystery and see the complete truth, or justice.

### Verse 2

**“Behold, a white horse.”** The Church whitened in baptism; or the greatest preachers, who carry God everywhere.

**“A bow.”** Christ possesses Scripture, with which he illuminates his own and kills his enemies.

### Verse 3

**“And when he had opened the second seal…”** Seeing the Church being established to fill the place from which he himself had fallen, the devil strives first to overthrow it openly.

**“A red horse.”** Contrary to the preceding one: namely, open and bloodthirsty persecutors.

### Verse 4

**“To take peace from the earth,”** and so forth. That is, it was granted by God that he should take away all peace of mind from those devoted to earthly things.

**“And a great sword was given to him.”** Great power to kill, because he dared to rage not only against the lesser but also against the greater, as against Peter.

### Verse 5

**“And behold, a black horse.”** Seeing that he had accomplished nothing through open persecutions, the devil sends heretics, who contend with false arguments so that they may deceive more easily.

**“A balance.”** Because they claim to possess true discernment in the Scriptures.

### Verse 6

**“And I heard something like…”** Because here, in the struggle with heretics, where the danger is greater, assistance is offered.

**“A two-pound measure.”** It is as though he said: “O faithful, do not fear those who were formerly able to harm you; and you, devils, do not harm these people, because you will not succeed, because two pounds of wheat…” and so forth.

**“Wheat.”** By wheat are understood the more perfect, who have been ground down by tribulation and cooked in fire, becoming pleasing food for God.

Barley signifies the lesser in the same category.

Wine signifies those who have indeed been crushed in the press, but not so thoroughly refined: they are merely sharp in themselves and intoxicate others for good works.

Oil signifies those who do not intoxicate others but first anoint them with prayers.

**“Do not harm the wine and the oil.”** That is, do not harm those who have been refreshed by wine—that is, by my blood—and anointed with oil—that is, with the Holy Spirit.

Wine likewise is bought for one denarius.

### Verse 8

**“Behold, a pale horse.”** Seeing that he could accomplish nothing either through open tribulations or through open heresies, the devil sends false brothers beforehand. Under the appearance of religion they possess the nature of the red and black horse, corrupting the faith.

**“Its name was Death.”** Because through it death came, or literally because it kills some in the flesh and others in the soul.

**“And Hades.”** That is, those insatiable for earthly things imitate him and are placed in hell.

**“Over the four…”** That is, over all the wicked dwelling everywhere; or over Jews and Gentiles, heretics and false Christians.

### Verse 9

**“And when…”** After the tribulations threatening the faithful in the present had been shown, he consoles those who suffer by giving them some assurance of the approaching crown, so that they may not fail.

**“I saw beneath the altar.”** That is, humbling themselves before their head; or “beneath,” meaning in concealment, because no one in this life perceives how they are there.

**“The altar.”** Christ, upon whom all the saints offer themselves and in whom they have protection. Or the souls themselves are the altar from which pleasing smoke proceeds to God. Since they had been stained with blood, they now exist beneath—that is, in a lower dignity than they will have in the future—because they have not yet received more than one robe.

**“Those slain for the word.”** Either through open martyrdom or through certain anxieties—

### Verse 10

**“How long?”** The saints desire greater joy and fellowship with the saints, and they agree with God’s justice in the condemnation of the impious.

**“Do you judge and do not avenge the blood…”** By making a distinction between the good and the evil.

### Verse 11

**“Their fellow servants.”** They are called servants on account of the Lord himself, brothers through love; they must wait.

### Verse 12

**“The sun became black.”** That is, those in whom it shines will be reckoned guilty and sinful while retaining their own brightness; or because some will fall into darkness.

Or Christ, the true sun, who is now bright, will be dark at the time of the Antichrist—that is, shining with no miracles.

**“Like a sackcloth.”** When light is placed in a sack, it does not shine outside. On this day of great tribulation, the faithful will not pour out the light of preaching.

### Verse 13

**“Its unripe figs.”** That is, empty fruits. For God allows nothing to fall that serves him with true love.

### Verse 14

**“The heaven.”** That is, the Church will withdraw from the wicked in faith and works. Hence: “Come out of Babylon, my people, and do not touch what is unclean.”

### Verse 15

**“The kings of the earth.”** According to the various honors of the world, which they are unwilling to lose and therefore destroy the faith.

**“The rich.”** Those who fulfill whatever evil they desire.

**“The strong.”** Those who are strong in overthrowing others.

A slave of sin, free in righteousness: these, despairing of help from the saints, seek the aid of demons, so that those in whom they trusted may free them.

### Verse 16

**“And they say to the mountains…”** Let them seek the intercession of the angels, who are more eminent mountains and rocks in firmness, so that through their prayers they may obtain the judge’s mercy.

## Chapter VII

### Verse 1

**“After this,”** and so forth. Having described the Church’s manifold warfare, he adds that during this warfare the devil is prepared to do harm but is restrained by God, so that his own people may not become sluggish or despair.

**“Four angels.”** For the four parts of the world in which they cause harm.

**“Angels.”** The devil is called an angel—that is, one sent by God for the testing of the good and permitted for the deception of the wicked—and is sent by the devil, their prince, for the overthrow of all.

**“Holding.”** In a time of tribulation nothing is more necessary than preaching, and therefore the devil strives to hold it back everywhere.

**“The winds.”** Wind raises clouds, waters the earth, makes it fruitful, and gives it a cheerful appearance. So preaching affects human minds.

**“Upon the sea.”** Upon those dwelling in islands, or upon those overflowing with various vices.

### Verse 2

**“And I saw another…”** This angel is the stone cut without hands, which shattered the statue composed of four metals. He is the one who released the four winds.

**“Ascending.”** After Christ expired, he ascended when he bound the devil and illuminated the world through preachers by faith, like the sun by its light.

Or he ascended from the east—that is, from the Father—advancing in wisdom and age.

Or he descended from himself, because he did not assume flesh through intercourse with a man; rather, he himself created it, he who is the rising of the sun, that is, of the Father.

**“A sign.”** That is, the cross by which he would mark his own; or power equal to the Father; or freedom from sin, through which God appears, because every human being is a sinner.

Although the ancient fathers bore this sign not in reality, they bore it in faith.

The sign is carried on the forehead so that it may not be concealed in tribulation. The marking of the breast is confession of the heart. When an infant is catechized, he is anointed on the breast so that he may have faith in his heart, and on the forehead so that he may not blush but confess: “With the heart one believes unto righteousness, but with the mouth confession is made unto salvation” (Rom. X).

It is placed on the shoulders so that he may bear Christ’s burden. It is placed on the crown of the head so that he may preserve reason, which is the crown and head of the inner person.

[Col. 0724A]

### Verse 4

**“One hundred and forty-four thousand.”** He gives a fixed number because God comprehends all his own within a definite number.

**“From every tribe.”** That is, from all who imitate Jacob in faith.

### Verse 5

**“Twelve.”** Through the number twelve we have those who are marked by faith in the Trinity in the four parts of the world. To show them as perfect, we multiply twelve by four, producing forty-eight. To refer this perfection to the Trinity, we multiply forty-eight, and thus produce one hundred and sixty-four.

### Verse 7

**“Simeon.”** “Hearing of sadness” or “of grief”: that is, grieving over past sins and aspiring to a life of virtue.

**“Levi.”** That is, “added”: namely, doing even what was not imposed upon him.

**“Issachar.”** That is, “reward”: namely, striving toward recompense, as in, “I desire to depart and to be with Christ.”

### Verse 8

**“Zebulun.”** That is, “dwelling of strength”: those who do not refuse labor but sometimes, out of necessity for the brethren, descend from Mary to Martha.

**“Joseph.”** That is, “increase”: those who enrich the Church by the number of the saints.

**“Benjamin.”** That is, “son of the right hand”: those who attribute everything to God’s favor and regard nothing as coming from themselves.

### Verse 9

**“After this.”** Having seen those who were to be designated figuratively by a fixed number, and only from the sons of Israel, he now openly teaches that by this number all the faithful are understood, and by the twelve tribes all the nations.

**“Standing.”** Namely, prepared to obey God the judge, or even their own prelates.

This refers to the present time.

### Verse 10

**“Salvation belongs to our God who sits…”** We possess salvation—not through ourselves but through the Lamb—that is, remission of sins, good works, and eternal glory.

### Verse 11

**“And all…”** Through the angels mentioned above, the greater prelates may be understood; through these, the lesser prelates, or merely the subjects. This is like the distinction between angels and archangels, although all are angels—that is, messengers.

In the present age also there are greater and lesser prelates, namely archbishops and bishops.

### Verse 12

**“Amen.”** It is as though he said: “If you attribute these things to God, you do well.”

Or “amen” may be joined to what follows: “Amen,” that is, truth in the preceding statements; “blessing,” that is, the exaltation he possesses above every creature, or our exaltation in virtues; and “glory,” that is, freedom from suffering, or your glory in works.

### Verse 13

**“And one answered…”** Having seen the crowd in such great dignity, he is moved to ask by what way it could have ascended there, so that he may teach others to examine the same matter.

### Verse 14

**“Their robes,”** and so forth. The innocence received in baptism, or their bodies.

### Verse 16

**“They will hunger no more, nor thirst anymore,”** and so forth. He who gave knowledge to the angels will also give them the same knowledge.

### Verse 17

**“He will lead them to the waters of life,”** and so forth. Through this, in the future, he will lead them to complete refreshment.

**“God will wipe away every tear.”** Every grief, whether arising from their sins, from adversities, from exile, or from other things of this kind.

## Chapter VIII

### Verse 1

**“And when he had opened…”** In this life’s third vision, seven angels are seen sounding trumpets for the destruction of enemies, in the likeness of those who, sounding trumpets, destroyed the walls of Jericho.

It is as though he said: “When I had understood the salvation of the righteous, on the other hand I understood the condemnation of the impious through the office of preaching entrusted to the good.”

## CHAPTER VIII

### Verse 2

**“Seven angels.”** All of them, or those imbued with the sevenfold Spirit. **“And they were given.”** Because God is not displeased by the damnation of the wicked.

### Verse 3

**“And another angel.”** The angel stood before the altar, prepared to sacrifice, in the likeness of a priest; or Christ is the altar who offered himself, and upon whom the Church offers prayers to God. He stood before the altar—that is, before himself—because he has no mediator through whom he might be pleasing.

**“Having.”** About to declare that the damnation of the wicked would come from the preaching of the righteous, he first offers something like an excuse, lest they be blamed for the damnation of the wicked, since, as far as they were concerned, their preaching was good and had been imposed upon them by a good teacher.

**“A censer.”** That is, the apostles, who are vessels of fire, namely, of the Holy Spirit, and from whom prayers go forth, rising before God.

**“Of the prayers.”** He said “of the prayers,” and not “the prayers,” because he does not present all prayers to the Father, but hears those that pertain to salvation. He says “of the prayers” because they sometimes ask for what ought not to be asked, as Paul did.

**“Upon the golden altar.”** That is, upon the one who is above himself according to his humanity, in which respect he is the altar of the Trinity.

### Verse 4

**“Smoke.”** The compunction produced by devotion to prayer, kindled inwardly by the fire of the vision of God.

### Verse 6

**“They prepared.”** That is, they first fulfilled in deed what they were going to say with their mouths. Or, “they prepared” means that they foresaw what was appropriate for each person.

**“And the first angel.”** In the order of the narrative, or because this blindness of the Jews first occurred when the apostles were preaching.

### Verse 7

**“And hail came to be.”** That is, preaching which was sweet to others appeared to them dense and burdensome.

**“Upon the earth.”** The Jews are like earth cultivated by the Law and the Prophets.

**“Of the trees.”** By the trees are understood the greater Jews, who conducted themselves blamelessly in the Law.

### Verse 8

**“And the second angel.”** The second according to the order of the narrative and according to the order in which it was fulfilled. For after the Jews had been blinded, the apostles turned to the Gentiles.

**“Into the sea.”** The Gentiles are the sea, that is, flowing into many vices. Although the devil was already among them, he is nevertheless rightly said to have been cast into them, because, when some withdraw, he strives to retain others.

### Verse 9

**“A third part died.”** Two parts—that is, all the good—believed; the third part—that is, all the reprobate—were given over to a depraved mind.

**“Those which had souls,”** and so forth. That is, those Gentiles who were regarded by others as more worthy on account of certain good works.

### Verse 10

**“And the third angel.”** The third according to the order of the narrative and because this occurred after the other two. For after the devil was unable to blind all the Jews and Gentiles, he sent heretics among them and overturned some of them.

**“The fountains.”** They are called fountains because the highest point and, as it were, the origin of the whole faith is contained in them, as in the Gospel. The rivers drawn from them are their interpretations, in which there are two senses belonging to the faithful: the historical and the allegorical. There is a third, belonging to heretics, when they confirm their heresies by perverse interpretations of the Scriptures.

### Verse 12

**“And the fourth angel.”** He is called the fourth according to the order of the narrative and according to the order of events. For when the devil had blinded some of the Jews and Gentiles, he finally went forth to attack the very sons of the Church, and seized some of them, both the greater and the lesser.

He narrated these four condemnations as past, since they are seen daily in the churches. But he causes three future ones to be foretold, in order to teach that in the last times even more serious dangers than those of the past are impending. This may also be applied to the consolation of those living in the present.

### Verse 13

**“Of one eagle.”** The eagle signifies all preachers who, with minds raised far above, behold things from afar and, going around the Church, strengthen it by predicting the future. Here they are all one because they strive toward the same end.

## CHAPTER IX

### Verse 1

**“And the fifth angel.”** According to the order of the narrative and the order of time, this angel is said to be the fourth. For this is the condemnation of those whom the devil sends to prepare the way before the face of Antichrist.

**“And I saw a star.”** That is, the flame of the heretics, of which he had said a little earlier; he now explains by what fuel it grew.

**“A star.”** That is, the devil falling and striving so that no one might enter his place—that is, paradise.

**“And there was given.”** The abyss—that is, the place of darkness. The well—that is, the deeper heretics, because they plunge others beneath the surface by their perverse opinions. He is said to receive the key over these—that is, authority—because at that time he will not be restrained by God as he is now. Or, those keys are the very princes through whom the heretics operate.

### Verse 2

**“He opened the well of the abyss.”** He caused the heresies that lay hidden in their hearts to be brought forth.

**“The smoke of the furnace.”** The teaching of Antichrist is rightly called smoke, because Antichrist himself is the furnace that purifies the good and reduces the wicked to ashes.

**“The sun and the air were darkened.”** As a result, some who were illuminating others were struck, and some who had been illuminated by them were struck as well.

### Verse 3

**“Locusts came out.”** The disciples of the heretics are compared with locusts because they neither fly upward—that is, toward contemplation through knowledge—nor walk firmly through good works. Rather, they leap through pride, fall back into worse things, and consume what is good.

**“As scorpions have.”** A scorpion, gentle in appearance, secretly stings with its tail; or he compares them to a scorpion because, just as a scorpion deceives with its tail, so heretics deceive through temporal things, which ought to come afterward, just as the tail is the posterior part of an animal. Or he compares them for this reason: when a scorpion stings, it is not felt, but afterward it spreads its poison; so those deceived by heretics do not perceive it and finally perish.

### Verse 4

**“It was commanded them not to harm,”** and so forth. God restrains the deceits of these people, even though they themselves do not understand it.

### Verse 5

**“That they should not kill.”** When heretics are unable by their deceits to overturn those whom they wish to overturn, God has ordained this against them: even if they kill bodies, they may not deceive souls.

**“For five months.”** Another manuscript reads “for six months,” on account of the six ages by which this life is divided.

**“Like the torment of a scorpion.”** Although the power to torment has been given, they do not torture openly, but accuse people before the rulers of the world.

### Verse 6

**“And death will flee from them.”** Because care for the flock binds them to labor.

### Verse 7

**“The likenesses of the locusts,”** and so forth. Having shown how they harm—both by deceit and by hidden attack—and having shown God’s restraint in both matters, he now shows what those beings themselves are like through whom they are able to operate.

**“Like horses.”** Because they are swift in roaming about, fierce in attacking, and do not consider whom they encounter, whether neighbors or enemies.

**“As crowns.”** That is, victories acquired over those who have been overthrown and subverted, not through true wisdom.

### Verse 8

**“And they had hair.”** That is, lascivious and effeminate conduct, which clings to them and hangs from them for the deception of others. Or the hair signifies lesser men, whom they deceive by making them adhere to themselves.

**“The teeth of lions.”** They have tearing and stench.

### Verse 9

**“Breastplates.”** That is, obstinate hearts which the arrow of truth does not penetrate. Or, opinions fortified by deceptions, which truth shatters.

**“Like the sound of chariots,”** and so forth. Different chariots are driven along different roads by different horses toward the same battle. So these people, through different heresies, attack the Church with one accord.

### Verse 10

**“And they had tails.”** When their reasoning or tumult is of no avail, they seek the help of rulers, who are called tails because, in order to bind people, they frighten and flatter them. Or the tails are deceitful opinions with which they flatter openly and sting secretly.

### Verse 11

**“And they had a king over them.”** Having shown what they are in themselves, he shows through whom these things are possible.

**“Whose name in Hebrew is Abaddon.”** As if he were saying: “For this reason beware, Hebrews, Greeks, and Latins”—that is, the whole Church. He mentioned three languages because the Gospel of Christ was written and received in some form in each of these three languages.

### Verse 12

**“One woe has gone forth.”** That is, the first in the order of the narrative and in the order of time. This is the disclosure and condemnation of the wicked that will take place in the time of Antichrist.

### Verse 13

**“From the four horns.”** By the four horns understand the four things that are preached about Christ: his birth, passion, resurrection, and ascension; other matters are connected with these.

**“Of the golden altar.”** The altar is Christ; the horns of the altar are the preachers who exalt Christ and are prepared to die for him, just as blood was placed upon the horns of the altar. Or the altar is the Church, in which there are horns—that is, defenders of others—all striving toward the same end. Or by the four horns we may understand the evangelical teachings that teach the exposure of the frauds of Antichrist.

**“One voice.”** The heralds of the past warn those who will exist in the time of Antichrist.

### Verse 14

**“Release the four.”** On account of the four parts of the world, or because they attack the four things preached about Christ.

**“Who are bound in the great river Euphrates.”** The Euphrates is the river surrounding Babylon; that is, it signifies the worldly rulers through whom the devil, while present in them, worked secretly. By saying “Release,” he commands that these rulers be excommunicated, so that the one who was, as it were, bound in them may work more openly through those handed over to him.

Or the four angels are all the unclean spirits reigning in the four parts of the world, who were restrained in the passion of Christ.

### Verse 15

**“They were released,”** and so forth. When the devil is released, many are thrown headlong; they strive to blind others.

**“For the hour and day.”** By “hour” understand half a year; by “day,” one year; by “month,” another year; and by “year,” a third. For the persecution of Antichrist will last three and a half years.

### Verse 16

**“Twenty thousand times ten thousand.”** The saints, perfected by the ten commandments of the Law, are opposed by a twofold number of wicked people, because the wicked are more numerous than the good.

**“And I heard,”** and so forth. As if he were saying: “I rightly place them under a definite number, because I heard”—that is, I understood—that the wicked were more numerous than the good.

### Verse 17

**“And thus I saw.”** Just as I had understood that they rode forth for the destruction of others, so I understood that they did this through the devil, whom they carried as horses carry riders. Or the horses may be understood as devils, upon whom the wicked are founded.

**“They had fiery breastplates.”** That is, they fortified them with opinions from which eternal punishment follows, where there is fire, stench, and smoke. Or they had fiery breastplates—that is, eternal punishment, which never releases those whom it receives.

**“Like the heads of lions.”** Earlier, in the plague of the locusts, he saw human faces; here, lions’ faces. Heretics display something of humanity, but the ministers of Antichrist will compel people by punishments to confess what they teach by words and signs.

**“Fire proceeded.”** This signifies the cause of eternal punishment. Or fire signifies desire, smoke pride, and sulfur the stench of evil works.

**“Smoke and sulfur.”** They are blind and placed in darkness because of the stench of vices and evil works.

### Verse 18

**“A third part was killed.”** That is, all the reprobate from the Church, and likewise all Jews or pagans who were never baptized and were never separated from the Church.

### Verse 19

**“Like serpents.”** They flatter with their faces and secretly inject poison.

## CHAPTER X

### Verse 1

**“And I saw another strong angel.”** Because the Strong One, armed, overcame the strong devil.

**“From heaven.”** That is, from the knowledge of the angels.

**“Clothed with a cloud.”** That is, humbling himself by assuming flesh; or because he made himself knowable. He was hidden in flesh, which is refreshment for us against vices.

**“And a rainbow upon his head.”** Whoever has true knowledge of God regards him as God.

**“Like a pillar of fire.”** These are those in whom the image of God truly shines, as in contemplatives; or it signifies preaching.

### Verse 2

**“And he had in his hand a little open book.”** That is, all the Scriptures fulfilled through his action: partly by preaching, partly by completing what had been said about him, and finally by opening their meaning to his own people.

**“His foot.”** That is, firm bearers in the faith who support others.

**“But his left foot upon the earth.”** That is, upon those who supported others in some way, even though they did not believe.

This means that he placed the greater and stronger preachers over the greater sinners, and the lesser over the lesser.

### Verse 3

**“As when a lion roars.”** The voice of the lion displays his power and produces terror. When a lion makes a furrow with his tail around the forest and roars, none of the wild beasts dares to come out. So Christ, enclosing his own within the faith, roars lest anyone go out.

### Verse 4

**“I was about to write.”** Here he assumes the role of those who will wish to preach in the time of Antichrist by imitating their predecessors.

**“The signs that spoke.”** This signifies divine inspiration or an angelic admonition.

### Verse 5

**“He raised his hand toward heaven.”** When such desolation will exist in the Church that even preaching will be taken away, the faithful hear, for their consolation and not to the detriment of their salvation, that preaching is being withdrawn.

### Verse 6

**“He swore,”** and so forth. By this he firmly established the matter, because he was God. For “if Christ has risen, we too shall rise” (1 Cor. 15).

**“And the things that are in it.”** When you say, “He created the things that are in it,” you overthrow the heresy of certain people who assert that some things were not created by God but by the devil, such as a toad.

**“Time will be no more.”** That is, there will be no variation, but eternal stability and the immortality of souls. Considering this, those who come last will endure willingly.

### Verse 7

**“The mystery will be completed.”** In the time of Antichrist there will be such persecution that preaching will be forbidden to those who live at that time, even if they wish to preach and even if they are to receive the office of preaching from their predecessors. Others, however, preached this same message because they had been appointed for it by Christ.

Christ appointed them because it was then the time for preaching and because he had come for that purpose. But now observe the destruction of the time of Antichrist, contrary to the destruction that Christ brought about, and thereby understand that preaching is rightly withdrawn.

**“The mystery of God.”** That is, the reward of the saints, which is a secret “that eye has not seen and ear has not heard” (1 Cor. 2).

### Verse 8

**“As he proclaimed the Gospel.”** The first concern of the prophets was the coming of the Lord and the consummation of the age.

### Verse 9

**“And I heard.”** As if he were saying: Having shown the destruction that will occur in the time of Antichrist, and consequently the withdrawal of preaching, and having thereby provided consolation for the faithful, he is instructed to preach in the meantime what he has seen. It is as if he were told openly:

“Behold, I have revealed everything to you. Now go and preach, and do not avoid these things because they are harsh. Do not be terrified by any tribulation, because you will not suffer as much as those who persevere in the time of Antichrist.”

This is placed here for the consolation of the present Church, where a greater tribulation is foretold.

**“Go.”** Since he knew this well, he is instructed to understand it, so that through the admonition others who will preach may be formed.

**“Of the one standing upon the sea.”** He says this because it is difficult for humanity—which is soft and fragile—to fulfill such a command.

### Verse 10

**“And I went.”** He says this because, when God sees someone prepared, he freely offers what is necessary.

**“To the angel.”** That is, to the Scripture completed by God and disclosed among the faithful.

### Verse 11

**“And he said to me: You must,”** and so forth. When I received the book, even though I understood it to be bitter, he instructed me not to abandon it even on account of death.

## CHAPTER XI

### Verse 1

**“Measure.”** That is, preach according to the capacity of each person, so that you establish the Church and in it an altar, and so forth.

### Verse 2

**“The outer court.”** That is, false Christians, who pretend to be the Church but deny it by their deeds.

**“The holy city.”** That is, the Church gathered for righteous living and imbued with virtues. They will persecute it for forty-two months—that is, for three and a half years, during which Antichrist will reign.

It is as if he were saying: “Know that all the persecutions which exist in the present and which existed in the past proceed from Antichrist, just as those which will occur in his own time.”

### Verse 3

**“And I will give to the two.”** As if he were saying: When the tribulation is lesser, you must not cease, because when the time of greater tribulation comes, I will make them preach.

**“To the two witnesses.”** Elijah and Enoch are meant; through them other preachers are understood.

**“For a thousand days.”** Note that these days do not complete three and a half years, just as Christ did not complete half a year of preaching beyond three years.

### Verse 6

**“Over the waters.”** That is, over teachings which are waters irrigating the faithful.

**“Into blood,”** and so forth. Into sin—either when what is heard is neglected or when people refuse even to hear it.

### Verse 8

**“Egypt.”** That is, darkness without knowledge of God.

### Verse 10

**“And they will send gifts.”** That is, gifts literally; or congratulations and conversations with one another about them.

### Verse 11

**“And after the days.”** Having shown their tribulation, by whose example the angel invited John to preach, even if it should be necessary for him to suffer with them, he nevertheless also shows their crowns, so that he may likewise assure this John—or anyone else—of his own crown according to his measure.

**“Upon their feet.”** That is, upon themselves, who had previously needed something upon which to lean, but who will then be firm.

### Verse 12

**“A loud voice.”** One that refreshes them and terrifies their enemies.

### Verse 13

**“A great earthquake.”** That is, earthly people were shaken so that they might be punished in hell; or, after the teachers had been killed, it signifies the destruction of the Church.

**“And a tenth part.”** That is, a human being who appears to have been appointed so that the tenth order might be restored.

**“Were killed in the earthquake.”** They were utterly destroyed in hell, or afterward they did not repent.

**“Glory to God.”** That is, praises to God for the salvation of the righteous and the damnation of the wicked.

### Verse 15

**“And the seventh angel,”** and so forth. The first six trumpets, compared with the ages of the present world, announced various attacks in the wars of the Church. The seventh, heralding the eternal Sabbath, indicates only the victory and dominion of the true King.

**“It has come to pass.”** The one who was previously vile and rejected now reigns, crowning the good and condemning the wicked.

**“And he will reign.”** That is, his kingdom will endure forever—not, as certain heretics think, that the saints will return to the life of the world after a determined period.

### Verse 16

**“And the twenty-four elders.”** Not only do the lesser glorify God in this way, but the greater do so as well.

**“They fell upon their faces.”** The one who recognizes guilt in this life and laments it through repentance falls upon his face. The one who falls backward is the person who suddenly falls away in this life and does not know to what punishments he is being led.

### Verse 18

**“Those who corrupted the earth.”** That is, themselves through evil conduct, and others through bad example.

### Verse 19

**“And it was opened.”** In this fourth vision you have material well arranged and provided with good assistance: namely, the struggle of the Church, which is attacked by the devil both openly and secretly. In all these matters John shows that the Church prevails, by which he especially arms the faithful so that they may not fail in any tribulation.

The knowledge of the Church’s struggle therefore depends upon the third vision, which concerns the imposed duty of preaching.

**“The temple of God was opened.”** That is, the Holy Spirit was given, through whom the mysteries of the Church—which had been represented by the second tabernacle—were revealed to the faithful.

**“The ark.”** Christ is the ark in whom all the treasures of wisdom are hidden. He completed the Old Testament and instituted the New.

**“And great hail.”** That is, preaching appeared intolerable to some.

## CHAPTER XII

### Verse 1

**“And a sign.”** From these things I saw this proceeding—namely, the grace of faith, signifying something great.

Here he mentions the revelation of the mysteries that belonged to the second vision, and the imposed duty of preaching that we had in the third, in order to show that this fourth vision, concerning the struggle of the Church and the devil, depends upon those two—that is, the second and the third.

**“The moon beneath her feet.”** Although the Church is supported by worldly things, she does not desire them.

**“And upon her head a crown,”** and so forth. That is, the twelve apostles, through whom the world believed, or in whom the Church conquered the world.

### Verse 2

**“She is in labor so that she may give birth.”** She suffers adversity through preaching. Or she is in labor by herself—that is, she mortifies her flesh so that preaching may be effective.

### Verse 3

**“A great dragon.”** He speaks not of the greatness of the dragon’s effect but of its power and pride.

**“And ten horns,”** and so forth. That is, the kingdoms and riches by which rulers attack the Decalogue of the Law.

### Verse 4

**“And his tail.”** That is, deceptions by which they conceal vices, just as shameful things are concealed by the tail.

**“Of the stars.”** That is, of those who illuminate the Church by teaching, but not by their lives.

**“He stood before the woman.”** She was suffering pain, through which he believed that she would soon yield. Through her suffering the devil believed that the Church had been subjected.

**“To devour.”** The dragon was prepared to devour her, but he could not, because the one who prevented it was born.

### Verse 5

**“And she gave birth.”** By carnal generation, Christ proceeded from Abraham and David. Or the Church gave birth to a son—that is, to the faith of Christ in the hearts of those who hear.

### Verse 6

**“For a thousand days.”** That is, throughout the entire time during which the Church endures through the preaching of Christ, carried out for three and a half years.

### Verse 7

**“Michael and his angels fought.”** They sustain the Church by praying and bringing assistance.

### Verse 8

**“They did not prevail.”** They could not remove the assistance of the angels, because they will not be able to lead the Church into sin.

### Verse 10

**“And I heard a voice.”** Having shown that the devil was defeated in this hidden contest by the Church through the assistance of the Son and the angels, he adds the rejoicing of those angels themselves—or of the holy souls—over the victory of their brothers, so that those who hear angels or holy souls rejoicing over their victory may labor to conquer.

**“He accused them.”** It is the devil’s office to accuse—that is, to make people liable to accusation through sin.

**“Day and night.”** By delighting them in prosperity and distressing them in adversity.

### Verse 12

**“The devil came down.”** From heaven; or from the lesser saints, in whom temptation no longer has a place.

**“Knowing that he has little time.”** Because he sees many being taken away from him and placed in his position.

**“And after he saw.”** When the devil saw that he could not advance through hidden fraud, he attacked in order to conquer through open tribulation.

**“And there was given to the woman,”** and so forth. Against open tribulation also she has assistance from the same Son from whom she had assistance against hidden attack.

### Verse 14

**“Eagles.”** Those who seek heaven through the conduct of their lives are called eagles, and for that reason they keep their gaze fixed upon God.

**“For a time, and times,”** and so forth. If the condition of that Church which will exist in the time of Antichrist is intended, “for a time, and times, and half a time” will be understood in another way, in reference to the preaching of Elijah and Enoch. If the time of the universal Church is intended, “for a time, and times, and half a time” is understood differently, in reference to the preaching of Christ, carried out for three and a half years, because the Church is nourished daily by Christ’s preaching.

### Verse 16

**“And the earth helped the woman.”** That is, Christ gave his Church strength to suffer.

**“And opened”—that is, prepared—and made itself fit to receive whatever might be brought against it, like someone opening his mouth. Christ did this in his passion, in which he set before his own an example of suffering.

**“It swallowed up.”** That is, he destroyed all punishments in himself, becoming immortal and incapable of suffering. He does the same in his own people.

### Verse 17

**“The dragon became angry with the woman.”** Although he cannot overcome her, he does not cease to envy her and to seek an opportunity to attack.

### Verse 18

**“And he stood.”** Yet he did not conquer all those lesser ones. He stood only upon the sand—that is, he lingered among the fruitful, in whom signs of his footprint appeared.

## CHAPTER XIII

### Verse 1

**“And I saw,”** and so forth. Spiritually, this beast is Antichrist; or, in general, the whole collection of the wicked.

**“Seven heads and ten horns.”** In order to be able to overcome these people successfully, he established such a household for himself.

**“Names of blasphemy.”** The beast was full of various heresies, or concealing vices through various simulations.

### Verse 3

**“As though slain.”** Antichrist will pretend to be dead, and after hiding for three days he will appear, saying that he has been raised.

**“And the wound of his death was healed.”** By magic art he will ascend into the air, carried by demons, and thus his wound of death will be healed. For previously he was believed to be dead, but afterward he will be regarded as living.

### Verse 6

**“And he opened his mouth.”** He burst forth into such confidence that what he had previously dared to blaspheme secretly, he then dared to blaspheme publicly.

**“And the tabernacle.”** That is, his entire institution, through which he appears worthy of praise.

### Verse 8

**“He was slain from the foundation of the world.”** In his own people, as in Abel. Or because it was determined before all things that he would be slain at the end of time. Or he was mystically slain in the lamb that Abel offered; or he was prefigured in Abel himself, who was killed by his brother.

### Verse 10

**“Who leads into captivity.”** He who now takes human beings captive from the faith and eventually from salvation—namely, Antichrist, or the devil himself.

**“Who kills with the sword.”** Antichrist and his followers kill with the material sword and with persuasion, and they will perish by the sword of eternal judgment.

**“Here is,”** and so forth. That is, the saints will hold fast to patience and faith because, after he has been destroyed, they know that they will be rewarded. By looking upon the punishment of the wicked and the reward of the good, they become patient and hold fast to the faith.

### Verse 11

**“And I saw.”** Having described the tribulation that will come through Antichrist and his associates, he adds another that will come through his apostles, whom he will scatter throughout the whole world.

**“Horns.”** Because they will pretend to possess innocence, pure conduct, true teaching, and miracles—things that Christ possessed and gave to his own. Or they will claim the two Testaments for themselves.

**“And he spoke like a dragon.”** That is, the false apostles will speak as the devil had spoken in Antichrist.

### Verse 12

**“And authority,”** and so forth. Because in all things they placed Antichrist, their head, above themselves.

**“The earth.”** That is, earthly people who persist in love of the earth; or “the earth” according to the body, while they inhabit it according to the soul.

**“To adore.”** For these people too, by means of a pretended resurrection, make it the foundation of their preaching, just as Christ’s apostles did.

### Verse 13

**“Fire.”** That is, he will cause an evil spirit to descend upon his followers, so that they may speak in various languages. Just as the Holy Spirit was given to the apostles in the form of fire, so they will give an evil spirit in the form of fire.

**“In the presence.”** So that everyone may be able to see, since the apostles received the Holy Spirit in an enclosed room.

### Verse 15

**“So that the image might speak.”** By magical art he will make a statue speak and foretell the future.

### Verse 16

**“To have the mark,”** and so forth. They will place signs on the hand and on the forehead, so that everyone may confess in word and deed that he is their god.

### Verse 17

**“The number.”** That is, those who expect from him a reward that is lesser, moderate, or greatest.

### Verse 18

**“Whoever has.”** Since the present book has been published in Greek, the number must be sought according to the Greeks, among whom all the letters signify numbers.

His name is **Antemos**, which suits one who is called contrary to Christ: **A**, one; **N**, fifty; **T**, four hundred; **E**, five; **M**, forty; **O**, seventy; **S**, two hundred.

Or **Arnoyme**, that is, “I deny,” the one who denies that Christ is God; it has the same number: **A**, one; **R**, two hundred; **N**, fifty; **O**, seventy; **Y**, four hundred; **M**, forty; **E**, five.

Or **Teian**, that is, “the giant sun,” which, although properly belonging to Christ, is applied by usurpation to Antichrist: **T**, three hundred; **E**, five; **I**, ten; again **T**, three hundred; **A**, one; **N**, fifty.

Or in Latin letters: **Diclux**, because he will say that he himself is the light: **D**, five hundred; **I**, one; **C**, one hundred; **L**, fifty; **V**, five; **X**, ten—and thus the same total.

Six is the first perfect number, and signifies those who are less perfect, namely, married people who observe the ten commandments according to their measure.

Sixty signifies those who are moderately perfect: they remain chaste after dismissing lawful marriages, and again fulfill the ten commandments according to their measure.

One hundred signifies the most perfect, who do not violate the integrity of mind or body and observe the ten commandments most perfectly.

These produce fruit: some thirtyfold, others sixtyfold, and others a hundredfold. At that time the disciples of Antichrist will say that no one can be saved unless they offer Antichrist one of those fruits.

## CHAPTER XIV

### Verse 1

**“And I saw; and behold, the Lamb was standing.”** Having shown the extremely serious persecution that the Church will suffer from Antichrist and his apostles, he now shows what kind of helper she has and what kind of household he himself has, so that he may console the afflicted elect more fully.

**“One hundred and forty,”** and so forth. That is, the most perfect in virginity, gathered from the four parts of the world in the faith of the Trinity.

### Verse 2

**“Of thunder.”** Because they terrify those who flee to come into their fellowship.

**“Of harpists.”** Because they appointed themselves for this purpose: to stretch their devoted hearts upon the wood of the cross.

**“Playing the harp.”** What they possessed as an office, they fulfilled in action.

### Verse 3

**“And they were singing.”** That is, they will rejoice in the integrity of soul and body. Their joy will never grow old, but will always be new to them.

### Verse 4

**“These are the ones who are not with women.”** That is, those whom the blood of Christ raised up so that they might be virgins.

**“First fruits from human beings,”** and so forth. As the finest horse is chosen from a herd, or first fruits from among fruits.

### Verse 6

**“And I saw.”** Having described the attack carried out through the two beasts, and having set forth the assistance of the Lamb and shown the dignity of his household, he adds an admonition that people should approach this household, and a warning that they should withdraw from the other.

**“Another angel.”** That is, preachers who are other than Christ—that is, carrying out his role.

**“Through the midst of heaven.”** Through the catholic Church, which they draw along with themselves by words and examples.

**“An eternal Gospel.”** That is, preaching that promises eternity and leads those who observe it to eternity.

### Verse 7

**“Fear the Lord,”** and so forth. By doing good and proclaiming him rightly, so that he may appear glorious through you.

**“Because the hour has come.”** As if he were saying: “Do not fail, because you will suffer for only a short time.”

### Verse 8

**“And another angel followed him.”** He says this because preachers succeed one another.

**“Fallen.”** The word “fallen,” repeated twice, signifies an utter fall, in which complete destruction is understood.

**“With the wine of the wrath of her fornication.”** That is, with vices, and especially idolatry, which is a sweet drink to sinners. Through it they defile others and intoxicate them so that they may not walk along the straight path; therefore God’s wrath is owed to them.

Pure wine is drunk when God scourges people here for correction; turbid wine is drunk when eternal damnation is inflicted.

### Verse 9

**“And the third angel.”** He names three on account of the faith of the Trinity, although these three things can be considered in the same person.

### Verse 10

**“Which is mixed.”** As if he were saying: Whoever is not corrected by the punishment given for correction will be punished with eternal punishment.

**“In the cup.”** The cup is God’s vengeance. In it, above, is pure wine, by which he punishes here for correction; beneath is the dregs, namely damnation at the end.

The wicked will drink wine—that is, the dregs. Since he wishes to show that this wine is turbid in comparison with the pure wine, he adds that it is mixed.

### Verse 11

**“And the smoke of their torments.”** When he enumerates certain features of the damnation of the wicked, he does not do so to describe the damnation itself, but only to instill terror in those whom he deters from their company.

**“It will rise forever.”** By saying “it will rise forever,” he indicates that eternal punishment continues.

**“Nor do they have rest.”** As if to say: It is not surprising that those who worshiped Antichrist in his time will be punished, because his preceding ministers will also suffer the same punishment.

### Verse 12

**“Here is patience,”** and so forth. That is, here the saints must suffer patiently, lest they come to eternal punishment.

### Verse 13

**“Works.”** That is, the rewards of the works which follow.

As if he were saying: While they were in the world, greater tribulations pressed upon them for a greater crown; therefore they were regarded as so utterly rejected. But now they will suffer nothing.

### Verse 14

**“And I saw.”** Having shown the reward of the good, by which he invited people to their company, he adds the damnation of the wicked, so that through terror he may lead them to the same purpose.

**“Like the Son of man.”** Because he was no longer truly the Son of man, since he was immortal.

### Verse 15

**“The angel.”** That is, the saints, who had until then been hidden among the faithful, will appear in glory to judge, praying with desire that God may separate the good from the wicked.

**“He came out of the temple.”** The saints are said to come out of the temple when they appear no longer as they once were, but as they will remain forever.

**“Because the hour has come,”** and so forth. Because the appropriate time has arrived, since the number of your own has been completed.

### Verse 18

**“And another angel,”** and so forth. After Saint John had shown that the saints implored God, who possesses the power to judge, and that judgment was thus carried out, he shows that the saints themselves possess the same authority, that Christ commands them to judge, and that they obey his command.

**“Another angel.”** That is, Christ, who had been hidden and regarded as lowly, appeared glorious among the faithful. He came from the altar—that is, from a more secret place—from which no other saint ever came; for Christ alone is known by all as consubstantial with God.

**“Send the sickle.”** By the harvest of the earth and the grapes of the vine is understood the damnation of the same wicked people. Nevertheless, by the vineyard we have a more precise designation of those who practiced evil with greater zeal, since a vineyard requires greater care to produce fruit than the earth does.

### Verse 19

**“And he cast it into the lake,”** and so forth. Hence the Prophet says: “A lake where there was no water”—that is, no refreshment.

**VERSE 20.**—“And blood came out.” The eternal punishment for the sin of bloodshed is meant; it is not wine that is placed in God’s storeroom. “As far as the horses’ bridles,” that is, as far as the very rulers of the wicked who are to be punished, namely, the devils. “For a distance of stadia.” Understand all who are held by the games of the world, that is, by vices: some are simply perfect in this respect, which is signified by six; others more perfect, by one hundred; and the most perfect, by one thousand.

## CHAPTER XV

**VERSE 1.**—“And I saw,” etc. In the three visions mentioned above—namely, the revelation of mysteries, the giving of the trumpets, and the woman’s struggle against the devil—he followed the sequence from the beginning of redemption up to the day of judgment. In the three that follow, however, he dwells on the final times, because the matters treated in the earlier visions have been explained more fully in other divine Scriptures, whereas these matters are treated only briefly and more obscurely.

In this fifth vision, therefore, the subject is seven angels holding bowls, in which are contained plagues, that is, the destructions of the wicked who will exist in the time of Antichrist [Col. 0737A]. This destruction chiefly urges those now living to endure suffering.

In what follows he sets forth three visions, although four were mentioned above. Omitting the first, which concerned the correction of the churches, he speaks of the other three, though with consideration. “And a sign of wonder.” It is wondrous that a human being should possess such power that he can condemn others. “Seven plagues,” that is, all of them: the blinding and destruction of those who will exist in the time of Antichrist. “Because in them.” They will truly have plagues, because they will exercise God’s wrath against the wicked; and they will truly be the last, because after them God will inflict no others upon the world.

**VERSE 2.**—“Like a glassy sea mingled with fire.” That is, baptism, in which purity of faith is required and human beings are cleansed from vices. “Having harps,” that is, mortifying the flesh, as God commanded them, or as he himself first did [Col. 0737B].

**VERSE 3.**—“The song of Moses.” That is, the old Law; and it is the rejoicing of those who understand rightly, that is, spiritually. “Ways,” that is, God’s ordinances, by which we come to God or he comes to us, are just because they repay each person according to merit, and true because they lead to the place they promise.

**VERSE 4.**—“Your judgments,” etc. The fact that you choose some and reject others is so that the faithful may know that this proceeds from justice.

**VERSE 5.**—“And after these things.” When they had shown that those angels possessed the power to inflict plagues, and he was about to state what plagues they would bring upon them, he first sets forth the reason, showing that they were worthy to suffer the plagues.
